sentences.zh: 25%劉子玄劉子玄，名知幾，以玄宗諱嫌，故以字行。

translations.literal: Liu Zixuan—Liu Zixuan, personal name Zhiji; because of taboo against the character Ji shared with Emperor Xuanzong's name, he was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixuan, whose personal name was Zhiji, avoided using it because it tabooed Emperor Xuanzong's given name, and was therefore known by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 年十二，父藏器為授《古文尚書》，業不進，父怒，楚督之。

translations.literal: At age twelve, his father Cangqi taught him the Old Text Book of Documents, but his progress was poor; his father grew angry and lashed him with a cane.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve, his father Cangqi had him study the Old Text version of the Book of Documents, yet he made little progress, and his father, enraged, beat him with a cane.

sentences.zh: 及聞為諸兄講《春秋左氏》，冒往聽，退輒辨析所疑，嘆曰：「書如是，兒何怠！

translations.literal: When he heard that his elder brothers were being lectured on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, he would steal in to listen; upon returning he would parse their doubts and sigh, saying: "If books are like this, how can the boy be idle!"
translations.idiomatic: When he overheard his elder brothers being taught the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, he would slip in to listen; afterward he would work through their questions and exclaim, "If learning is like this, how could a boy be lazy!"

sentences.zh: 」父奇其意，許授《左氏》。

translations.literal: His father marveled at his intent and permitted him to be taught the Zuo [Commentary].
translations.idiomatic: His father, struck by the boy's keenness, allowed him to study the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遂通覽群史。

translations.literal: Within a year he had read through the histories in full.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he had read his way through the entire corpus of historical works.

sentences.zh: 與兄知柔俱以善文詞知名。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Zhirou were both renowned for fine literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Zhirou were both celebrated for their skill in literary writing.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，調獲嘉主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Huojia.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was posted as chief clerk of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 武后證聖初，詔九品以上陳得失。

translations.literal: In the first year of Empress Wu's Zhengsheng reign, an edict ordered officials of the ninth rank and above to present the strengths and failings [of government].
translations.idiomatic: Early in Empress Wu's Zhengsheng era, an edict called on officials of the ninth rank and above to submit critiques of what was working and what was not.

sentences.zh: 子玄上書，譏「每歲一赦，或一歲再赦，小人之幸，君子之不幸」。

translations.literal: Zixuan submitted a memorial ridiculing [the practice]: "An amnesty every year, or twice in a year—is the petty man's blessing and the gentleman's misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan submitted a memorial attacking the practice: "An amnesty every year, or twice in one year, is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's misfortune."

sentences.zh: 又言：「君不虛授，臣不虛受。

translations.literal: He also said: "The ruler should not bestow honors without cause; ministers should not receive them without merit."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "A ruler must not grant rewards without cause, and ministers must not accept them without merit."

sentences.zh: 妄受不為忠，妄施不為惠。

translations.literal: To receive groundlessly is not loyalty; to grant groundlessly is not kindness.
translations.idiomatic: To accept rewards one has not earned is not loyalty; to hand them out without cause is not benevolence.

sentences.zh: 今群臣無功，遭遇輒遷，至都下有『車載鬥量，杷椎碗脫』之諺。

translations.literal: "Today the ministers achieve nothing yet on every chance are promoted; in the capital there is even a saying: 'Cartloads by the bushel—ladles and bowls worn smooth.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Today officials achieve nothing yet are promoted at every turn, until in the capital people say, 'They come by the cartload and are measured by the bushel—ladles and bowls worn smooth with use.'"

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「刺史非三載以上不可徙，宜課功殿，明賞罰。

translations.literal: He also said: "Prefects should not be transferred before three full years; merit should be assessed and rewards and punishments made clear."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Prefects should not be transferred before they have served three full years; their performance should be evaluated, and rewards and punishments should be made explicit."

sentences.zh: 」后嘉其直，不能用也。

translations.literal: The Empress praised his forthrightness but could not employ his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress admired his blunt honesty but did not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 時吏橫酷，淫及善人，公卿被誅死者踵相及。

translations.literal: At the time officials were brutal and cruel, harm reaching even good men, and among the highest ministers those executed followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at the time were brutal and overbearing, and even the virtuous suffered; among the highest ministers, those put to death followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 子玄悼士無良而甘於禍，作《思慎賦》以刺時。

translations.literal: Zixuan mourned that scholars lacked good judgment yet acquiesced in disaster, and wrote "Rhapsody on Thinking Cautiously" to satirize the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan grieved that men of learning lacked sound judgment yet resigned themselves to ruin, and wrote the "Rhapsody on Thinking Cautiously" to satirize his times.

sentences.zh: 蘇味道、李嶠見而嘆曰：「陸機《豪士》之流乎，周身之道盡矣！

translations.literal: Su Weidao and Li Jiao read it and sighed: "In the vein of Lu Ji's 'Heroic Gentleman'—the way to preserve oneself is fully set forth!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao and Li Jiao read it and exclaimed: "This is in the line of Lu Ji's 'Heroic Gentleman'—the art of keeping oneself whole is fully laid out!"

sentences.zh: 」子玄與徐堅、元行沖、吳兢等善，嘗曰：「海內知我者數子耳。

translations.literal: Zixuan was on close terms with Xu Jian, Yuan Xingchong, Wu Jing, and others, and once said: "Within the realm only a few such men know me."
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan was close to Xu Jian, Yuan Xingchong, Wu Jing, and others, and once said: "Under heaven, only a handful of men truly know me."

sentences.zh: 累遷鳳閣舍人，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, concurrently compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, while also serving on the staff compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，擢太子率更令。

translations.literal: Under Zhongzong he was advanced to Director of the Heir Apparent's Office of the Director of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong he was promoted to Director of the Heir Apparent's Office of the Director of Music.

sentences.zh: 介直自守，累歲不遷。

translations.literal: Upright and self-restrained, he went many years without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Scrupulous and self-contained, he went many years without advancement.

sentences.zh: 會天子西還，子玄自乞留東都。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned west, Zixuan requested of his own accord to remain in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned west to Chang'an, Zixuan asked on his own initiative to remain in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，或言子玄身史臣而私著述，驛召至京，領史事。

translations.literal: In the third year, someone said that though Zixuan was a historiographer he engaged in private writing; he was summoned posthaste to the capital to head historiographical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, someone reported that although Zixuan was a court historian he was also writing on his own; he was summoned by urgent relay to the capital to take charge of historiography.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時宰相韋巨源、紀處訥、楊再思、宗楚客、蕭至忠皆領監脩，子玄病長官多，意尚不一，而至忠數責論次無功，又仕偃蹇，乃奏記求罷去。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers Wei Juyuan, Ji Chuna, Yang Zaisi, Zong Chuke, and Xiao Zhizhong all supervised the compilation; Zixuan was troubled that there were too many superiors and their views did not agree, while Zhizhong repeatedly blamed them for making no progress in ordering the text; moreover his own career had stalled, so he submitted a memorial asking to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief ministers Wei Juyuan, Ji Chuna, Yang Zaisi, Zong Chuke, and Xiao Zhizhong all held supervisory roles over the history project. Zixuan was vexed by the multitude of superiors and their lack of a unified vision, while Zhizhong repeatedly reproached the staff for failing to advance the compilation; with his own career also at a standstill, he submitted a memorial requesting release from the post.

sentences.zh: 因為至忠言「五不可」，曰：「古之國史，皆出一家，未聞藉功於眾。

translations.literal: He therefore set forth to Zhizhong the "five impossibilities," saying: "The national histories of antiquity all came from a single hand; one never hears of borrowing the labor of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore explained to Zhizhong the "five impossibilities," saying: "The state histories of old were all the work of a single author; one never hears of farming out the task to a crowd."

sentences.zh: 唯漢東觀集群儒，纂述無主，條章不建。

translations.literal: Only in Han did the Eastern Pavilion gather many Confucians; compilation had no master and regulations were not established.
translations.idiomatic: Only under the Han did the Eastern Pavilion assemble many scholars, with no one in charge of the compilation and no clear rules established.

sentences.zh: 今史司取士滋多，人自為荀、袁，家自為政、駿。

translations.literal: Today the historiographical office recruits ever more men; each man is his own Xun [Yue] or Yuan [Hong], each household its own Sima [Qian] or Ban [Gu].
translations.idiomatic: Today the history office recruits ever more staff, until every man fancies himself a Xun Yue or Yuan Hong and every household its own Sima Qian or Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 每記一事，載一言，閣筆相視，含毫不斷，頭白可期，汗青無日：一不可。

translations.literal: Whenever one event is to be recorded or one remark entered, pens are laid aside and eyes meet; lips hold the brush but cannot decide—gray hair may be expected, yet the day of the green bamboo slips will never come: the first impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a single event is to be recorded or a single remark set down, pens are laid aside and eyes meet across the room; brushes are held in the mouth but no line is written—one may expect to grow old, yet the day the work is finished in ink will never come: the first impossibility.

sentences.zh: 漢郡國計書上太史，副上丞相，後漢公卿所撰，先集公府，乃上蘭臺，故史官載事為廣。

translations.literal: In Han the regional accounts were sent up to the Grand Historian with a copy to the Chancellor; in Later Han what the high ministers composed was first gathered in the public offices and only then sent to the Orchid Terrace—hence the historiographers' records were broad in scope.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, the regional statistical reports went up to the Grand Historian with a copy to the Chancellor; under Later Han, writings by the chief ministers were first collected in the government offices and only then sent to the Orchid Terrace. For this reason the historians' records were comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 今史臣唯自詢采，二史不註起居，百家弗通行狀：二不可。

translations.literal: Today the historians rely only on their own inquiries; the two [imperial] histories do not annotate the daily records, and the hundred families do not circulate their biographical accounts: the second impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Today the historians must gather material only by their own inquiries; the two imperial diaries are not annotated for them, and families do not circulate their official biographical accounts: the second impossibility.

sentences.zh: 史局深籍禁門，所以杜顏面，防請謁也。

translations.literal: The historiographical bureau lies deep within the forbidden gates in order to shut off face-to-face contact and guard against petitions.
translations.idiomatic: The history office lies deep within the palace gates precisely to cut off personal access and prevent lobbying.

sentences.zh: 今作者如林，儻示褒貶，曾未絕口，而朝野鹹知。

translations.literal: Today authors are thick as a forest; if praise or blame is even hinted at, before the words have left the mouth the court and commoners alike know it.
translations.idiomatic: Today writers are as numerous as trees in a grove; if praise or blame is even hinted at, before the words have left one's lips the whole court and countryside already know.

sentences.zh: 孫盛取嫉權門，王劭見讎貴族，常人之情，不能無畏：三不可。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng incurred the hatred of powerful families; Wang Shao made enemies among the nobility—ordinary human feeling cannot be without fear: the third impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng earned the enmity of powerful clans; Wang Shao made enemies among the aristocracy—given ordinary human nature, who can be without fear? The third impossibility.

sentences.zh: 古者史氏各有指歸，故司馬遷退處士，進奸雄；

translations.literal: In antiquity each historiographical house had its own orientation, so Sima Qian demoted recluses and advanced villainous heroes;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity each historian's house had its own bent, so Sima Qian downgraded recluses and elevated scheming strongmen;

sentences.zh: 班固抑忠臣，飾主闕。

translations.literal: Ban Gu suppressed loyal ministers and adorned the ruler's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu slighted loyal ministers and glossed over the sovereign's failings.

sentences.zh: 今史官註記，類稟監脩，或須直辭，或當隱惡，十羊九牧，其令難行：四不可。

translations.literal: Today the historians' annotations mostly take orders from the supervising compilers; sometimes straight words are needed, sometimes evils must be concealed—ten sheep, nine herdsmen: such an order is hard to carry out: the fourth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Today the historians' entries mostly follow instructions from supervising compilers; sometimes blunt truth is required, sometimes wrongdoing must be concealed—with ten sheep and nine shepherds, whose orders can be followed? The fourth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 今監者不肯指授，脩者又不遵奉，務相推避，以延歲月：五不可。

translations.literal: Today the supervisors will not give direction, the compilers will not obey, each striving to shift responsibility and stretch out the months: the fifth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Today the supervisors refuse to give clear guidance, the compilers refuse to follow it, and all parties push responsibility onto one another to drag out the months: the fifth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「朝廷厚用其才而薄其禮。

translations.literal: He also said: "The court makes heavy use of their talent but treats their rites lightly."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The court exploits their talent heavily while honoring their office lightly."

sentences.zh: 」至忠得書，悵惜不許。

translations.literal: Zhizhong received the letter, regretted it, and did not grant [the request].
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong received the memorial, was moved but regretful, and did not approve his resignation.

sentences.zh: 楚客等惡其言詆切，謂諸史官曰：「是子作書，欲致吾何地？

translations.literal: Chuke and the others hated his cutting words and said to the historians: "When this fellow writes his book, where does he mean to place us?"
translations.idiomatic: Chuke and his faction resented his sharp criticism and said to the other historians: "When this man writes his book, where does he intend to put us?"

sentences.zh: 始，子玄修《武后實錄》，有所改正，而武三思等不聽。

translations.literal: At first, when Zixuan revised the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he made corrections, but Wu Sansi and the others would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zixuan worked on the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he made corrections that Wu Sansi and his faction refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 自以為見用於時而誌不遂，乃著《史通》內外四十九篇，譏評今古。

translations.literal: Believing himself employed by the age yet his aims unfulfilled, he composed the Shitong in forty-nine inner and outer chapters, criticizing past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that although he was used by his times his historiographical aims had not been realized, he wrote the Shitong in forty-nine chapters, inner and outer, critiquing historians past and present.

sentences.zh: 徐堅讀之，嘆曰：「為史氏者宜置此坐右也。

translations.literal: Xu Jian read it and sighed: "Those who would be historians ought to keep this at their right hand."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian read it and exclaimed: "Anyone who would write history ought to keep this book at his right hand."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗自比楊雄者四：「雄好雕蟲小伎，老而為悔；

translations.literal: He also once compared himself to Yang Xiong in four respects: "Xiong delighted in petty ornamental craft and in old age repented of it;
translations.idiomatic: He also once drew four parallels between himself and Yang Xiong: "Xiong loved ornamental minor arts and repented of them in old age;

sentences.zh: 吾幼喜詩賦而壯不為，期以述者自名。

translations.literal: I in youth loved poetry and rhapsody but in maturity did not pursue them, intending to make a name as a writer of record."
translations.idiomatic: I delighted in poetry and rhapsody in youth but abandoned them in my prime, intending to make my name as a historian instead."

sentences.zh: 雄準《易》作經，當時笑之；

translations.literal: Xiong took the Changes as his model and wrote a classic; his contemporaries laughed at him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiong modeled a classic on the Changes and was mocked in his own day;

sentences.zh: 吾作《史通》，俗以為愚。

translations.literal: I wrote the Shitong, and the vulgar think me foolish.
translations.idiomatic: I wrote the Shitong, and ordinary people think me a fool.

sentences.zh: 雄著書見尤於人，作《解嘲》；

translations.literal: Xiong, when his books drew blame from others, wrote "Dispelling Ridicule";
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong's writings drew reproach, he wrote "Dispelling Ridicule";

sentences.zh: 吾亦作《釋蒙》。

translations.literal: I too wrote "Explaining Ignorance."
translations.idiomatic: I too wrote "Explaining Ignorance."

sentences.zh: 雄少為範逡、劉歆所器，及聞作經，以為必覆醬瓿；

translations.literal: Xiong in youth was prized by Fan Qun and Liu Xin; when they heard he was writing a classic, they thought it would surely end up covering a sauce jar;
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xiong was esteemed by Fan Qun and Liu Xin, but when they heard he was writing a classic they assumed it would end up covering a sauce jar;

sentences.zh: 吾始以文章得譽，晚談史傳，由是減價。

translations.literal: I at first won reputation through literary composition, but in later years spoke of historical transmission, and thereby my price fell.
translations.idiomatic: I first won fame through belles lettres, but when in later years I turned to historical writing, my reputation accordingly declined.

sentences.zh: 」其自感慨如此。

translations.literal: Such were his reflections on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the ways he lamented his own lot.

sentences.zh: 子玄內負有所未盡，乃委國史於吳兢，別撰《劉氏家史》及《譜考》。

translations.literal: Zixuan, inwardly burdened with what remained unfulfilled, entrusted the national history to Wu Jing and separately compiled the Liu Clan Family History and Genealogical Studies.
translations.idiomatic: Still inwardly burdened by what he had left undone, Zixuan handed the national history over to Wu Jing and set about writing separately the Liu Clan Family History and Genealogical Studies.

sentences.zh: 上推漢為陸終苗裔，非堯後；

translations.literal: Tracing upward, he held that the Han were descendants of Lu Zhong, not descendants of Yao;
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the line upward, he argued that the Han house descended from Lu Zhong rather than from Yao;

sentences.zh: 彭城叢亭裏諸劉，出楚孝王囂曾孫居巢侯般，不承元王。

translations.literal: the various Lius of Congting Lane in Pengcheng descended from Ban, Marquis of Juchao, great-great-grandson of Xiao, King of Chu, and did not derive from the King of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: and that the Liu clans of Congting Lane in Pengcheng descended from Ban, Marquis of Juchao, a great-great-grandson of King Xiao of Chu, rather than from the King of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 按據明審，議者高其博。

translations.literal: His evidence was clear and thorough, and debaters admired his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: His evidence was precise and thorough, and critics praised his learning.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾若得封，必以居巢紹司徒舊邑。

translations.literal: He once said: "If I receive a fief, it must be Juchao, continuing the old domain of the Minister of Works."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "If I am granted a fief, it must be Juchao, renewing the old domain of the Minister of Works."

sentences.zh: 」後果封居巢縣子。

translations.literal: Later he was indeed enfeoffed as Viscount of Juchao County.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was indeed enfeoffed as Viscount of Juchao County.

sentences.zh: 鄉人以其兄弟六人俱有名，號其鄉曰高陽，裏曰居巢。

translations.literal: The villagers, because all six brothers were famous, called their township Gaoyang and their lane Juchao.
translations.idiomatic: Because all six brothers were celebrated, their neighbors named the township Gaoyang and the lane Juchao.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子左庶子、兼崇文館學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and concurrently Academician of the Chongwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and concurrent Academician of the Chongwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皇太子將釋奠國學，有司具儀：從臣著衣冠，乘馬。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was to perform the libation at the National University, the offices prepared the rites: attendant ministers were to wear caps and robes and ride horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was to perform the libation at the National University, the relevant offices drew up the ritual: attendant ministers were to wear formal caps and robes while riding horses.

sentences.zh: 子玄議：「古大夫以上皆乘車，以馬為騑服。

translations.literal: Zixuan argued: "In antiquity grandees and above all rode in carriages, with horses as outriders.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan argued: "In antiquity officials of grandee rank and above all rode in carriages, with horses serving as outriders.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉後以牛駕車。

translations.literal: After Wei and Jin, oxen drew the carriages.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei and Jin periods, oxen were used to draw carriages.

sentences.zh: 江左尚書郎輒輕乘馬，則御史劾治。

translations.literal: In the southeast, if a Secretariat Gentleman casually rode a horse, the censor would impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: In the southeast, if a Secretariat Gentleman rode a horse lightly caparisoned, the censor would bring charges against him.

sentences.zh: 顏延年罷官，乘馬出入閭裏，世稱放誕。

translations.literal: Yan Yannian, after leaving office, rode a horse in and out of the lanes of his neighborhood, and the age called it unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Yannian left office, he rode a horse through his neighborhood lanes, and his contemporaries called it eccentric.

sentences.zh: 此則乘馬宜從褻服之明驗。

translations.literal: This is clear proof that riding a horse should follow informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: This is clear evidence that riding a horse should go with informal dress.

sentences.zh: 今陵廟巡謁、王公冊命、士庶親迎，則盛服冠履，乘輅車。

translations.literal: Today for touring imperial tombs and temples, for investiture of princes and dukes, and for commoners' wedding processions, full dress with cap and shoes is worn and the ceremonial carriage is used.
translations.idiomatic: Today, for visits to imperial tombs and temples, for the investiture of princes and dukes, and for commoners welcoming a bride, one wears full ceremonial dress with cap and shoes and rides in the state carriage.

sentences.zh: 他事無車，故貴賤通乘馬。

translations.literal: For other matters there is no carriage, so noble and humble alike commonly ride horses.
translations.idiomatic: For other occasions there is no carriage, so men of every rank commonly ride horses.

sentences.zh: 比法駕所幸，侍臣皆馬上朝服。

translations.literal: Recently, when the imperial procession went forth, attendant ministers all wore court dress on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the imperial procession set out, attendant ministers all wore court dress on horseback.

sentences.zh: 且冠履惟可配車，故博帶褒衣、革履高冠，是車中服。

translations.literal: Moreover caps and shoes can only be paired with carriages; hence the broad belt, full robe, leather shoes, and tall cap are dress for riding in a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, caps and shoes belong only with carriages; the broad belt, full robe, leather shoes, and tall cap are clothing meant for riding in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 襪而鐙，跣而鞍，非唯不師於古，亦自取驚流俗。

translations.literal: Socks with stirrups, bare feet with saddle—this not only fails to follow antiquity but also startles common custom of its own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing socks in stirrups or going barefoot against the saddle not only breaks with ancient practice but also shocks ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 馬逸人顛，受嗤行路。

translations.literal: When horses bolt and men are thrown, they are mocked in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: When horses bolt and riders are thrown, passersby laugh.

sentences.zh: 」太子從之，因著為定令。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince followed his advice and had it written as a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince accepted his view and had it enacted as a fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗議《孝經》鄭氏學非康成註，舉十二條左證其謬，當以古文為正；

translations.literal: He once argued that the Zheng-school learning of the Classic of Filial Piety was not the commentary of Kangcheng, citing twelve proofs of its error, and that the Old Text version should be authoritative;
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that the Zheng-school tradition of the Classic of Filial Piety was not Zheng Xuan's commentary, offering twelve proofs of its errors, and that the Old Text version should be authoritative;

sentences.zh: 《易》無子夏傳，《老子》書無河上公註，請存王弼學。

translations.literal: that the Changes had no Zixia transmission and the Laozi had no commentary by the Duke of the River—requesting that Wang Bi's learning be retained.
translations.idiomatic: that the Changes had no transmission from Zixia and the Laozi had no commentary by the Duke of the River, and asked that Wang Bi's tradition be retained.

sentences.zh: 宰相宋璟等不然其論，奏與諸儒質辯。

translations.literal: The chief minister Song Jing and others did not accept his argument and memorialized for a debate with the Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Song Jing and others rejected his position and memorialized for a formal debate among the scholars.

sentences.zh: 博士司馬貞等阿意，共黜其言，請二家兼行，惟子夏《易傳》請罷。

translations.literal: The Erudites Sima Zhen and others curried favor, jointly rejected his words, and requested that both schools be followed together, asking only that the Zixia transmission of the Changes be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Sima Zhen and others flattered the court, jointly dismissed his views, and asked that both traditions be followed, requesting only that the Zixia transmission of the Changes be set aside.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 會子貺為太樂令，抵罪，子玄請於執政，玄宗怒，貶安州別駕。

translations.literal: When his son Kuang, as Director of the Imperial Music Office, incurred punishment, Zixuan pleaded with those in power; Xuanzong grew angry and demoted him to Vice-Prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Kuang, serving as Director of the Imperial Music Office, was convicted of an offense, Zixuan appealed to those in power; Emperor Xuanzong was angered and demoted him to Vice-Prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子玄領國史且三十年，官雖徙，職常如舊。

translations.literal: Zixuan headed the national history for nearly thirty years; though his offices changed, his duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan directed the national history for nearly thirty years; although his titles changed, his duties remained essentially the same.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書鄭惟忠嘗問：「自古文士多，史才少，何耶？

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zheng Weizhong once asked: "From antiquity literary men have been many and historiographical talent few—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Zheng Weizhong once asked him: "From antiquity there have been many men of letters but few true historians—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「史有三長：才、學、識。

translations.literal: He replied: "History has three excellences: talent, learning, and discernment."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "History demands three excellences: talent, learning, and discernment."

sentences.zh: 世罕兼之，故史者少。

translations.literal: The age rarely combines them, hence historians are few.
translations.idiomatic: Few men in any age combine all three, and that is why historians are rare.

sentences.zh: 夫有學無才，猶愚賈操金，不能殖貨；

translations.literal: To have learning without talent is like a foolish merchant handling gold yet unable to increase his goods;
translations.idiomatic: Learning without talent is like a dull trader who holds capital yet cannot turn a profit;

sentences.zh: 有才無學，猶巧匠無楩柟斧斤，弗能成室。

translations.literal: to have talent without learning is like a skilled craftsman without hardwood, axe, and adze, unable to complete a house.
translations.idiomatic: talent without learning is like a skilled craftsman without fine timber, axe, and adze, unable to finish a house.

sentences.zh: 善惡必書，使驕君賊臣知懼，此為無可加者。

translations.literal: Good and evil must be written so that arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers know fear—this is what nothing can surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil must be recorded so that arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers know fear—that is the historian's supreme duty.

sentences.zh: 」時以為篤論。

translations.literal: The age regarded it as sound doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries regarded this as profound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 子玄善持論，辯據明銳，視諸儒皆出其下，朝有論著輒豫。

translations.literal: Zixuan was skilled at holding arguments; his reasoning was clear and sharp, and he looked down on all the Confucians; whenever the court had a discourse he took part.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan excelled at debate; his reasoning was lucid and incisive, and he considered himself above the other scholars; whenever the court took up a question of doctrine, he was involved.

sentences.zh: 歿後，帝詔河南就家寫《史通》，讀之稱善。

translations.literal: After his death, the emperor ordered that the Shitong be copied at his home in Henan; he read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, the emperor ordered the Shitong copied at his home in Henan; on reading it, he praised the work.

sentences.zh: 追贈工部尚書，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and given the posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and given the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 六子：貺、餗、匯、秩、迅、迥。

translations.literal: Six sons: Kuang, Su, Hui, Zhi, Xun, and Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Kuang, Su, Hui, Zhi, Xun, and Jiong.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 貺貺，字惠卿。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Kuang, courtesy name Huiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Kuang, whose courtesy name was Huiqing.

sentences.zh: 好學，多通解。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had broad understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had wide-ranging understanding.

sentences.zh: 子玄卒，有詔訪其後，擢起居郎。

translations.literal: When Zixuan died, an edict sought out his descendants and promoted [Kuang] to Attendant for Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixuan's death, an edict sought out his descendants and promoted Kuang to Attendant for Drafting.

sentences.zh: 歷右拾遺內供奉。

translations.literal: He served successively as Right Reminder and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Right Reminder and Inner Attendant.

sentences.zh: 獻《續說苑》十篇，以廣漢劉向所遺，而刊落怪妄。

translations.literal: He presented "Continued Shuo Yuan" in ten chapters, to expand on what Han Liu Xiang left behind, and to delete the strange and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a ten-chapter Continuation of the Shuo Yuan to supplement what the Han scholar Liu Xiang had left incomplete, while excising fantastic and unreliable material.

sentences.zh: 貺嘗以《竹書紀年》序諸侯列會皆舉謚，後人追修，非當時正史。

translations.literal: Kuang once noted that in the preface to the Bamboo Annals, when the feudal lords are listed at their assemblies, all are given posthumous titles; later people revised it—it was not the official history of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang once argued that in the Bamboo Annals, the preface's lists of feudal lords at their gatherings all cite posthumous titles, showing that later hands had revised the text—it was not contemporary official history.

sentences.zh: 如齊人殲於遂，鄭棄其師，皆孔子新意，《師春》一篇錄卜筮事，與左氏合，知按《春秋》經傳而為也，因著《外傳》云。

translations.literal: Cases such as "the Qi people were destroyed at Sui" and "Zheng abandoned its army" were all new ideas of Confucius; the chapter "Shi Chun" records divination affairs, which agrees with the Zuo Commentary—knowing that it was compiled according to the Spring and Autumn classic and its commentary, he therefore wrote the Outer Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Passages like the destruction of the Qi at Sui and Zheng's abandonment of its army were all Confucius's own innovations; the "Shi Chun" chapter records divination, matching the Zuo Commentary—from which he knew the work was based on the Spring and Autumn canon and its commentaries, and so he wrote his Outer Commentary.

sentences.zh: 子滋、浹。

translations.literal: His sons: Zi and Jia.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zi and Jia.

sentences.zh: 貺子 滋滋，字公茂。

translations.literal: Kuang's son Zi, courtesy name Gongmao.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's son Zi, whose courtesy name was Gongmao.

sentences.zh: 通經術，喜持論。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics and their methods, and enjoyed holding forth in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He was thoroughly versed in the classics and loved to argue his views.

sentences.zh: 以蔭歷漣水令。

translations.literal: By inherited privilege he served successively as magistrate of Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he rose through the post of magistrate of Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 楊綰薦材堪諫官，累授左補闕。

translations.literal: Yang Wan recommended him as talent suited for a remonstrance office; he was repeatedly appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wan recommended him as qualified for remonstrance, and he was repeatedly appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 久之，去，養親東都。

translations.literal: After a long time he left office to care for his parents in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he resigned and went to the Eastern Capital to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 河南尹李廙奏補功曹，母喪解。

translations.literal: Henan Intendant Li Yi memorialized to appoint him administrative aide; upon his mother's death he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Intendant Li Yi petitioned to have him appointed chief clerk, but he resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服除，以司勛員外郎判南曹，勤職奉法，進至給事中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, as Deputy Director in the Ministry of Personnel he served in the Southern Bureau; diligent in duty and observant of law, he rose to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he served as Deputy Director of Personnel with charge of the Southern Bureau; diligent and law-abiding, he was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，以吏部侍郎知南選。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, as Vice Minister of Personnel he supervised the southern selection of officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xingyuan era, as Vice Minister of Personnel he oversaw official selection in the south.

sentences.zh: 時大盜後，旱蝗相仍，吏不能詣京師，故命滋至洪州調補，以振職聞。

translations.literal: At that time, after the great rebellion, drought and locusts followed one after another; officials could not reach the capital, so Zi was ordered to go to Hongzhou to adjust and fill vacancies, and became known for revitalizing his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the great rebellion, drought and locust plagues came in succession and officials could not travel to the capital, so Zi was sent to Hongzhou to adjust appointments and fill vacancies, earning a reputation for restoring order to his duties.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，擢左散騎常侍、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant and Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was elevated to Left Regular Attendant and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 為相無所設施，廉抑畏慎而已。

translations.literal: As chancellor he had nothing he could implement—only modesty, restraint, and caution.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he accomplished little beyond practicing modesty, restraint, and caution.

sentences.zh: 明年罷。

translations.literal: The following year he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 又明年，復為吏部侍郎，遷尚書。

translations.literal: Another year later, he again served as Vice Minister of Personnel and was transferred to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he returned as Vice Minister of Personnel and was then promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 會御史中丞韋貞伯劾奏：「吏選不實，澄覆疏舛，吏因得為奸。

translations.literal: When Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Zhenbo impeached: "Official selection is not truthful; screening and review are erroneous and contradictory, so officials thereby can commit malfeasance."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Zhenbo submitted an impeachment: "Official appointments are not honest, vetting and review are sloppy and contradictory, and clerks exploit the gaps to commit fraud."

sentences.zh: 」詔與侍郎杜黃裳奪階。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him and Vice Minister Du Huangshang of rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted both him and Vice Minister Du Huangshang in rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈陜州大都督，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored as Grand Governor of Shanzhou, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Governor of Shanzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 貺子 浹浹亦有學稱。

translations.literal: Kuang's son Jia also had a reputation for learning.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's son Jia was also known for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 生子敦儒，家東都。

translations.literal: He had a son Dunru; the family lived in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Dunru, and the family resided in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 母病狂易，非笞掠人不能安，左右皆亡去，敦儒日侍疾，體常流血，母乃能下食，敦儒怡然不為痛隱。

translations.literal: His mother suffered from madness; unless people were beaten she could not be settled, and all attendants fled; Dunru daily tended her illness, his body often streaming blood, yet only then could his mother eat—Dunru was at ease and did not conceal his pain.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was afflicted with violent madness and could not be calmed unless someone was beaten; all the attendants fled. Dunru attended her daily, his body often bleeding from her blows, yet only then would she eat—and Dunru bore it calmly, never showing his pain.

sentences.zh: 留守韋夏卿表其行，詔標闕於閭。

translations.literal: Left-behind Commissioner Wei Xiaqing memorialized his conduct; an edict marked his gate with an honor plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Left-behind Commissioner Wei Xiaqing memorialized his conduct to the throne, and an edict ordered a commemorative plaque erected at his gate.

sentences.zh: 元和中，權德輿復薦之，乃授左龍武軍兵曹參軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Quan Deyu again recommended him, and he was appointed Military Staff Officer of the Left Imperial Dragon Martial Guard, serving at the Eastern Capital branch.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era Quan Deyu recommended him again, and he was appointed military staff officer of the Left Imperial Dragon Martial Guard, serving at the Eastern Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 在母喪，毀瘠幾死。

translations.literal: During his mother's mourning he wasted away nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he grew so emaciated he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 時謂劉孝子。

translations.literal: At the time he was called the Filial Son Liu.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him Filial Son Liu.

sentences.zh: 後為起居郎，達禮好古，有祖風云。

translations.literal: Later he became Attendant of the Imperial Diary; versed in ritual and fond of antiquity, he had his grandfather's manner.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Attendant of the Imperial Diary; well versed in ritual and devoted to antiquity, he carried something of his grandfather's character.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 餗餗，字鼎卿。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Su, courtesy name Dingqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Su, whose courtesy name was Dingqing.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，歷集賢院學士，兼知史官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he served successively as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrently supervised the history office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era he served as an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrently oversaw the history office.

sentences.zh: 終右補闕。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 父子三人更蒞史官，著《史例》，頗有法。

translations.literal: Father and three sons in turn held posts as historians; they wrote "Historical Precedents," which had considerable method.
translations.idiomatic: Father and three sons served as historians in succession; they authored Historical Precedents, a work of considerable methodological rigor.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 匯匯，左散騎常侍，終荊南節度使。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Hui, Left Regular Attendant, ended as Military Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Hui, who had served as Left Regular Attendant, ended his career as military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 子贊，以蔭仕為鄠丞。

translations.literal: His son Zan, by inherited privilege entered service as Assistant Magistrate of E.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan entered office through hereditary privilege as assistant magistrate of E County.

sentences.zh: 杜鴻漸自劍南還，過鄠，廚驛豐給。

translations.literal: Du Hongjian returning from Jiannan passed through E; the kitchen and post-house supplies were abundantly provided.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Hongjian returned from Jiannan and passed through E, Zan lavishly supplied his kitchen and post station.

sentences.zh: 楊炎薦匯名儒子，擢浙西觀察判官。

translations.literal: Yang Yan recommended Hui's son, scion of a famous Confucian, and he was promoted to administrative officer under the Zhexi Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan recommended him as the son of the renowned scholar Hui, and he was promoted to administrative officer under the Zhexi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 炎入相，進歙州刺史，政幹強濟。

translations.literal: When Yan entered the chancellorship, Zan was advanced to Prefect of Shezhou; his governance was forceful and effective.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan became chief minister, Zan was promoted to prefect of Shezhou, where his administration was vigorous and effective.

sentences.zh: 野媼將為虎噬，幼女呼號搏虎，俱免。

translations.literal: An old woman in the wild was about to be devoured by a tiger; a young girl cried out and fought the tiger—both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: An old peasant woman in the countryside was about to be killed by a tiger when a young girl screamed and fought the tiger off—they both escaped unharmed.

sentences.zh: 觀察使韓滉表贊治有異行，加金紫，徙常州。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner Han Huang memorialized that Zan's administration had extraordinary conduct; he was granted golden seal and purple robe and transferred to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Observation Commissioner Han Huang memorialized Zan's extraordinary conduct in office, and Zan was awarded the golden seal and purple robe and transferred to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 滉輔政，分所統為三道，以贊為宣州刺史、都團練觀察使，治宣十年。

translations.literal: When Huang assisted in government, he divided what he controlled into three circuits and appointed Zan Prefect of Xuanzhou and Overall Training Commissioner and Observation Commissioner; he governed Xuan for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang entered the central government, he divided his jurisdiction into three circuits and appointed Zan prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training and observation commissioner; Zan governed Xuan for ten years.

sentences.zh: 贊本無學，弟以剛猛立威，官吏重足一跡。

translations.literal: Zan originally had no learning; he and his younger brother established authority through stern ferocity—officials walked as if on tiptoe, fearing to leave a trace.
translations.idiomatic: Zan had little learning of his own; he and his younger brother ruled through harsh severity, and officials were so terrified they scarcely dared to move.

sentences.zh: 宣既富饒，即厚斂，廣貢奉以結恩。

translations.literal: As Xuan was already rich and fertile, he heavily levied taxes and broadly sent tribute to cultivate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was already prosperous, so he levied heavy taxes and sent lavish tribute to court to win favor.

sentences.zh: 又不能訓子，皆驕傲不度，素業衰矣。

translations.literal: He also could not instruct his sons—all were arrogant and unrestrained, and the family's longstanding enterprise declined.
translations.idiomatic: He also failed to discipline his sons, who grew arrogant and unrestrained, and the family's longstanding reputation declined.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 迥迥以剛直稱，第進士，歷殿中侍御史，佐江淮轉運使。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Jiong was known for firm uprightness; he passed the jinshi examination, served successively as Palace Investigating Censor, and assisted the Jiang-Huai Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Jiong was known for his firm integrity; a jinshi graduate, he served as palace investigating censor and assisted the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時新更安史亂，迥饋運財賦，力於職。

translations.literal: At that time, freshly after the An-Shi rebellion, Jiong supplied and transported wealth and taxes, exerting himself in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the immediate aftermath of the An Lushan rebellion, Jiong worked tirelessly to supply and transport revenue and provisions.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，為吉州刺史，治行尤異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dali, he was Prefect of Jizhou; his conduct in governing was especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali era he served as prefect of Jizhou, where his record of governance was especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 秩秩，字祚卿。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Zhi, courtesy name Zuoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zuoqing.

sentences.zh: 開元末，歷左監門衛錄事參軍事，稍遷憲部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, he served successively as Clerk of the Left Gate Guard; he gradually rose to Deputy Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Kaiyuan period he served as clerk of the Left Gate Guard and gradually rose to deputy director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坐小累，下除隴西司馬。

translations.literal: For a minor offense he was demoted to military adjutant of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a minor infraction he was demoted to military adjutant of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，哥舒翰守潼關，楊國忠欲奪其兵，秩上言：「翰兵天下成敗所系，不可忽。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Geshu Han defended Tong Pass; Yang Guozhong wished to seize his troops; Zhi submitted a memorial: "Han's army is bound up with the success or failure of the empire—it must not be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Geshu Han held Tong Pass while Yang Guozhong sought to strip him of his command; Zhi submitted a memorial: "General Han's army holds the fate of the empire in the balance—it must not be treated lightly."

sentences.zh: 」房琯見其書，以比劉更生。

translations.literal: When Fang Guan saw his memorial, he compared him to Liu Gengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan, reading the memorial, compared Zhi to Liu Gengsheng.

sentences.zh: 至德初，遷給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, he was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhide era he was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為閬州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was sent out as Prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was sent out to serve as prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 貶撫州長史，卒。

translations.literal: Demoted to senior administrator of Fuzhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to senior administrator of Fuzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 所著《政典》、《止戈記》、《至德新議》等凡數十篇。

translations.literal: His writings included "Administrative Canon," "Record of Ceasing Arms," "New Discussions of the Zhide Era," and several dozen other works.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included the Administrative Canon, Record of Ceasing Arms, New Discussions of the Zhide Era, and several dozen other works.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 迅迅，字捷卿。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Xun, courtesy name Jieqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Xun, whose courtesy name was Jieqing.

sentences.zh: 歷京兆功曹參軍事。

translations.literal: He served successively as administrative aide of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrative aide of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 常寢疾，房琯聞，憂不寐，曰：「捷卿有不諱，天理欺矣！

translations.literal: Often ill in bed, when Fang Guan heard of it he was worried and could not sleep, saying: "If Jieqing meets with misfortune, Heaven's principle will be deceived!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xun lay chronically ill, Fang Guan heard the news and lay awake in distress, saying: "If anything should happen to Jieqing, Heaven itself will have been deceived!"

sentences.zh: 」陳郡殷寅名知人，見迅嘆曰：「今黃叔度也！

translations.literal: Chen Commandery's Yin Yin was famed for knowing men; seeing Xun he sighed and said: "This is a Huang Shudu of our day!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yin of Chen Commandery, renowned for judging character, met Xun and sighed: "Here is a Huang Shudu for our age!"

sentences.zh: 」劉晏每聞其論，曰：「皇王之道盡矣！

translations.literal: Liu Yan whenever he heard his discourses would say: "The Way of emperors and kings is fully realized!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liu Yan heard him speak he would say: "The way of sage-kingship is fully embodied here!"

sentences.zh: 」上元中，避地安康，卒。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he fled to safety in Ankang and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era he took refuge in Ankang, where he died.

sentences.zh: 迅續《詩》、《書》、《春秋》、《禮》、《樂》五說。

translations.literal: Xun continued the Five Expositions on the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, Rites, and Music.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wrote continuations to the Five Expositions on the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, Rites, and Music.

sentences.zh: 書成，語人曰：「天下滔滔，知我者希。

translations.literal: When the book was finished, he told others: "The world runs on in confusion; few know me."
translations.idiomatic: When the work was complete he told others: "The world flows on in turmoil—few will understand me."

sentences.zh: 」終不以示人云。

translations.literal: In the end he never showed it to anyone.
translations.idiomatic: He never showed it to anyone before he died.

sentences.zh: 吳兢吳兢，汴州浚儀人。

translations.literal: Wu Jing—Wu Jing, a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少厲誌，貫知經史，方直寡諧比，惟與魏元忠、朱敬則遊。

translations.literal: In youth he sharpened his ambition, thoroughly knew the classics and histories, was upright and seldom found companions—he associated only with Wei Yuanzhong and Zhu Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he cultivated high ambition and mastered the classics and histories; upright and not given to casual alliances, he associated only with Wei Yuanzhong and Zhu Jingze.

sentences.zh: 二人者當路，薦兢才堪論撰，詔直史館，修國史。

translations.literal: When the two held power, they recommended Jing's talent suited for discussion and composition; an edict appointed him to the History Office to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When the two men came to power, they recommended Jing as qualified for scholarly writing; an edict appointed him to the History Office to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺內供奉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Reminder with inner palace attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Reminder with inner palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，改右補闕。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was changed to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era his title was changed to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 節閔太子難，奸臣誣構安國相王與謀，朝廷大恐。

translations.literal: During the crisis of Crown Prince Jiemin, treacherous ministers falsely framed the Prince of Guo as conspiring; the court was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis surrounding Crown Prince Jiemin, treacherous ministers falsely implicated the Prince of Guo in a conspiracy, throwing the court into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 兢上言：「文明後，皇運不殊如帶。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial: "After the Era of Civil Brilliance, the imperial fortune has been no wider than a belt."
translations.idiomatic: Jing submitted a memorial: "Since the Civil Brilliance era, the imperial house's fortunes have been as narrow as a belt."

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興，恩被骨肉，相王與陛下同氣，親莫加焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's dragon ascent showered favor on kin; the Prince of Guo shares your breath—no one is more closely related.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, you extended grace to your kin; the Prince of Guo shares your very breath—no one is closer to you in blood.

sentences.zh: 今賊臣日夜陰謀，必欲寘之極法。

translations.literal: Now the villainous ministers day and night secretly plot, determined to subject him to the utmost penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Now villainous ministers plot against him day and night, bent on having him punished by the severest law.

sentences.zh: 相王仁孝，遭荼苦哀毀，以陛下為命，而自托於手足。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guo is benevolent and filial; suffering bitterness and grief, he takes Your Majesty as his life and entrusts himself to you as to his own limbs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guo is benevolent and filial; crushed by grief, he holds Your Majesty as his very life and trusts himself to you as he would his own limbs.

sentences.zh: 若信邪佞，委之於法，傷陛下之恩，失天下望。

translations.literal: If you believe the wicked and hand him over to the law, you will wound Your Majesty's kindness and lose the empire's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: If you heed the wicked and surrender him to the law, you will wound your own kindness and forfeit the hopes of the empire.

sentences.zh: 芟刈股肱，獨任胸臆，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Cutting off your arms and legs to rely solely on your own breast—this is cause for chilling fear.
translations.idiomatic: To cut away your own arms and legs and rely only on your own judgment—this is something to chill the heart over.

sentences.zh: 自昔翦伐宗支，委任異姓，未有不亡者。

translations.literal: From antiquity, those who cut down the imperial line and entrusted power to unrelated surnames have never failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, dynasties that cut down their own clans and entrusted power to outsiders have never escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 秦任趙高，漢任王莽，晉家自相魚肉，隋室猜忌子弟，海內麋沸，驗之覆車，安可重跡？

translations.literal: Qin entrusted Zhao Gao, Han entrusted Wang Mang; the Jin house devoured its own flesh, the Sui court suspected its sons and brothers—the realm seethed; the overturned cart warns us—how can we follow the same track again?
translations.idiomatic: Qin placed trust in Zhao Gao, Han in Wang Mang; the Jin turned on their own kin, the Sui grew suspicious of their sons and brothers—and the realm boiled over. The overturned cart lies before us; how can we follow that same road again?

sentences.zh: 且根朽者葉枯，源涸者遊竭。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the root rots the leaves wither; when the source dries up the flow ceases.
translations.idiomatic: When the root rots, the leaves wither; when the source runs dry, the stream fails.

sentences.zh: 子弟，國之根源，可使枯竭哉！

translations.literal: Sons and brothers are the nation's root—can they be allowed to run dry!
translations.idiomatic: Sons and brothers are the root of the state—can we let that root wither away?

sentences.zh: 皇家枝幹，夷芟略盡。

translations.literal: The imperial house's trunk and branches have been nearly all cut down.
translations.idiomatic: The trunk and branches of the imperial house have been nearly cut away altogether.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位四年，一子弄兵被誅，一子以罪謫去，惟相王朝夕左右。

translations.literal: In the four years since Your Majesty took the throne, one son took up arms and was executed, one son was banished for crime—only the Prince of Guo remains day and night at your side.
translations.idiomatic: In the four years since Your Majesty's accession, one son took up arms and was put to death, another was banished for his crimes—only the Prince of Guo remains at your side day and night.

sentences.zh: 『鬥粟』之刺，《蒼蠅》之詩，不可不察。

translations.literal: The satire of "A peck of millet" and the ode "Blue flies"—these must not go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The satire of "Brothers quarreling over a peck of millet" and the ode "Blue Flies"—these warnings must not go unheeded.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下全常棣之恩，慰罔極之心，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty preserve the affection of constant osmanthus, comfort your boundless heart—how greatly the realm would be blessed!
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to preserve brotherly affection and comfort your boundless heart—the whole realm would be the better for it!

sentences.zh: 」累遷起居郎，與劉子玄、徐堅等並職。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Diary, serving alongside Liu Zixuan, Xu Jian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Attendant of the Imperial Diary, serving alongside Liu Zixuan, Xu Jian, and others.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初立，收還權綱，銳於決事，群臣畏伏。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first ascended, he gathered back the reins of power, was sharp in deciding affairs, and the ministers feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first took the throne, he reclaimed the reins of power, decided matters with sharp dispatch, and the ministers submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 兢慮帝果而不及精，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jing feared the Emperor was decisive but not sufficiently thorough, and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jing worried that the Emperor was decisive but not sufficiently careful in his judgments, and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 自古人臣不諫則國危，諫則身危。

translations.literal: From antiquity, if ministers did not remonstrate the state was endangered; if they remonstrated they themselves were endangered.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when ministers did not remonstrate the state fell into danger; when they did remonstrate they themselves fell into danger.

sentences.zh: 臣愚，食陛下祿，不敢避身危之禍。

translations.literal: I am foolish; receiving Your Majesty's salary, I dare not avoid the disaster of personal danger.
translations.idiomatic: I am a foolish man, but having eaten Your Majesty's salary I dare not shrink from the peril that remonstrance brings upon myself.

sentences.zh: 比見上封事者，言有可采，但賜束帛而已，未嘗蒙召見，被拔擢。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen those submitting sealed memorials—when their words had merit, they were only granted bolts of silk; they never received summons or promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have seen that when men submit sealed memorials with sound advice, they receive only a gift of silk—they are never summoned or promoted.

sentences.zh: 其忤旨，則朝堂決杖，傳送本州，或死於流貶。

translations.literal: If they went against the imperial will, they were beaten with rods in court and sent back to their prefectures, or died in exile and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: If they offended the throne, they were beaten with rods in open court and sent back to their home provinces, or died in exile.

sentences.zh: 由是臣下不敢進諫。

translations.literal: Hence subordinates dare not offer remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, officials below dare not speak up.

sentences.zh: 古者設誹謗木，欲聞己過；

translations.literal: In antiquity they set up a wood for criticism, wishing to hear their own faults;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity rulers erected a post for criticism so they might hear their own faults;

sentences.zh: 今封事，謗木比也。

translations.literal: today's sealed memorials are comparable to that criticism wood.
translations.idiomatic: sealed memorials today serve the same purpose as that post of criticism.

sentences.zh: 使所言是，有益於國；

translations.literal: If what is said is correct, it benefits the state;
translations.idiomatic: If what is said is right, the state is the better for it;

sentences.zh: 使所言非，無累於朝。

translations.literal: if what is said is wrong, it does no harm to the court.
translations.idiomatic: if what is said is wrong, the court is none the worse.

sentences.zh: 陛下何遽加斥逐，以杜塞直言？

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty so hastily reject and expel them, to block straight speech?
translations.idiomatic: Why then does Your Majesty so quickly reject and banish them, cutting off honest speech?

sentences.zh: 道路流傳，相視怪愕。

translations.literal: On the roads rumors spread; people look at each other in shock and dismay.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread along the roads, and people stare at one another in stunned disbelief.

sentences.zh: 夫漢高帝赦周昌桀、紂之對，晉武帝受劉毅桓、靈之譏，況陛下豁達大度，不能容此狂直耶？

translations.literal: The Han Emperor Gaodi pardoned Zhou Chang for a reply likening [the empress to] Jie and Zhou; the Jin Emperor Wudi accepted Liu Yi's mockery comparing him to the emperors Huan and Ling—how much more, then, should Your Majesty, open-handed and magnanimous, be able to tolerate this wild frankness?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han pardoned Zhou Chang even after he compared the empress to the tyrants Jie and Zhou; Emperor Wu of Jin accepted Liu Yi's barbs comparing him to the worthless emperors Huan and Ling. Surely Your Majesty, who is broad-minded and generous, can tolerate this blunt outspokenness as well?

sentences.zh: 夫人主居尊極之位，顓生殺之權，其為威嚴峻矣。

translations.literal: The lord of men occupies the highest position of honor and monopolizes the power of life and death; his authority is already formidable.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler sits at the apex of power and holds exclusive authority over life and death; his majesty is already awe-inspiring enough.

sentences.zh: 開情抱，納諫諍，下猶懼不敢盡，奈何以為罪？

translations.literal: If he opens his heart and accepts remonstrance, those below still fear and dare not speak fully—so how can it be made a crime?
translations.idiomatic: Even when the throne opens its heart to criticism, subordinates still hesitate to speak their minds fully. How, then, can frank speech be treated as a crime?

sentences.zh: 且上有所失，下必知之。

translations.literal: Moreover, when those above err, those below necessarily know it.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, whenever those above make mistakes, those below are sure to know.

sentences.zh: 故鄭人欲毀鄉校，而子產不聽也。

translations.literal: Therefore, when the people of Zheng wished to destroy the village school, Zichan would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, when the people of Zheng wanted to tear down the village school, Zichan refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 陛下初即位，猶有褚無量、張廷珪、韓思復、辛替否、柳澤、袁楚客等數上疏爭時政得失。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, Chu Wuliang, Zhang Tinggui, Han Sifu, Xin Tifou, Liu Ze, Yuan Chuke, and others still repeatedly submitted memorials debating the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first took the throne, men such as Chu Wuliang, Zhang Tinggui, Han Sifu, Xin Tifou, Liu Ze, and Yuan Chuke still submitted memorial after memorial debating the rights and wrongs of current policy.

sentences.zh: 自頃上封事，往往得罪，諫者頓少。

translations.literal: Recently, those who submitted sealed memorials have often been punished, and remonstrators have suddenly become fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, however, those who submit sealed memorials have often been punished, and the number of people willing to speak up has dropped sharply.

sentences.zh: 是鵲巢覆而鳳不至，理之然也。

translations.literal: This is like the magpie's nest overturned and the phoenix not arriving—it is the natural order of things.
translations.idiomatic: It is like overturning the magpie's nest so that the phoenix will not come—such an outcome follows naturally.

sentences.zh: 臣誠恐天下骨鯁士以讜言為戒，橈直就曲，斫方為刓，偷合茍容，不復能盡節忘身，納君於道矣。

translations.literal: I truly fear that upright men throughout the realm will take frank speech as a warning, bend the straight to the crooked, carve the square into the round, stealthily conform and temporize, and no longer be able to exhaust their loyalty, forget themselves, and guide the ruler onto the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that every outspoken man in the empire will take honest speech as a warning, bend what is straight to what is crooked, trim what is square into what is round, and quietly trim his words to please others—until no one can any longer give his full loyalty, risk himself without hesitation, and lead the ruler back to the right path.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王之德，莫盛於納諫。

translations.literal: Of an emperor-king's virtue, nothing surpasses accepting remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the virtues of an emperor, none is greater than the willingness to accept remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "When wood follows the line it becomes straight; when a ruler follows remonstrance he becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, "Wood that follows the carpenter's line becomes straight; a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「朝有諷諫，猶發之有梳。

translations.literal: " It is also said: "When the court has indirect remonstrance, it is like hair having a comb.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said, "When the court has indirect remonstrance, it is like hair having a comb."

sentences.zh: 猛虎在山林，藜藿為之不采。

translations.literal: When a fierce tiger is in the mountains and forests, even common greens are not gathered on its account.
translations.idiomatic: When a fierce tiger prowls the mountains and forests, people do not even gather common greens there.

sentences.zh: 」忠諫之有益如此。

translations.literal: " The benefit of loyal remonstrance is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the benefit of loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 自古上聖之君，恐不聞己過，故堯設諫鼓，禹拜昌言。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, the supremely sage rulers, fearing they would not hear their own faults, therefore Yao set up a remonstrance drum and Yu bowed to good words.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times, the greatest sage rulers feared that they might never hear of their own faults; that is why Yao set up a drum for remonstrance and Yu bowed in gratitude to good counsel.

sentences.zh: 不肖之主，自謂聖智，拒諫害忠，桀殺關龍逢而滅於湯，紂殺王子比幹而滅於周，此其驗也。

translations.literal: Unworthy rulers, deeming themselves sage and wise, rejected remonstrance and harmed the loyal: Jie killed Guan Longfeng and was destroyed by Tang; Zhou killed Prince Bi Gan and was destroyed by the Zhou—this is the proof.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy rulers, convinced of their own wisdom, rejected remonstrance and destroyed the loyal: Jie killed Guan Longfeng and was overthrown by Tang; Zhou killed Prince Bi Gan and was overthrown by the Zhou dynasty. History has proved the point again and again.

sentences.zh: 夫與治同道罔不興，與亂同道罔不亡。

translations.literal: Those who tread the same path as good order never fail to rise; those who tread the same path as chaos never fail to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow the ways of good government always prosper; those who follow the ways of disorder always perish.

sentences.zh: 人將疾，必先不甘魚肉之味；

translations.literal: When a person is about to fall ill, he first loses relish for the taste of fish and meat;
translations.idiomatic: When a person is about to fall ill, he first loses his appetite for fish and meat;

sentences.zh: 國將亡，必先不甘忠諫之說。

translations.literal: when a state is about to perish, it first loses relish for the teaching of loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: when a state is about to fall, it first loses its taste for loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，惟陛下深監於茲哉！

translations.literal: Alas, may Your Majesty deeply take heed of this!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, may Your Majesty take this deeply to heart!

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝驕矜自負，以為堯、舜莫己若，而諱亡憎諫。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui was arrogant and self-congratulatory, thinking neither Yao nor Shun could compare with him, and he dreaded [hearing of] ruin and hated remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui was proud and self-satisfied, believing that not even Yao or Shun could equal him, and he dreaded talk of ruin while loathing all remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「有諫我者，當時不殺，後必殺之。

translations.literal: He even said: "Whoever remonstrates with me—though I may not kill him on the spot, I will surely kill him later.
translations.idiomatic: He even declared, "Anyone who remonstrates with me may not die immediately, but I will kill him later."

sentences.zh: 」大臣蘇威欲開一言，不敢發，因五月五日獻《古文尚書》，帝以為訕己，即除名。

translations.literal: " The minister Su Wei wished to speak a word but dared not begin; on the fifth day of the fifth month he presented the Ancient Text Book of Documents, and the Emperor took it as satirizing himself and immediately stripped him of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: The minister Su Wei wanted to offer a word of advice but did not dare speak plainly; on the fifth day of the fifth month he presented the Old Text version of the Book of Documents, and the emperor took it as a personal satire and immediately stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀諫無伐遼，出為河池郡守。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu remonstrated against campaigning in Liaodong and was sent out to serve as prefect of Hechi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu remonstrated against the Liaodong campaign and was sent out to serve as prefect of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 董純諫無幸江都，就獄賜死。

translations.literal: Dong Chun remonstrated against visiting Jiangdu and was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chun remonstrated against the imperial visit to Jiangdu and was ordered to die in prison.

sentences.zh: 自是蹇諤之士，去而不顧，外雖有變，朝臣鉗口，帝不知也。

translations.literal: From then on, blunt-speaking men departed and did not look back; though changes arose externally, court ministers kept their mouths sealed, and the Emperor knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: After that, blunt-spoken men left and never looked back; though crises broke out beyond the palace, the court officials kept silent, and the emperor knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 身死人手，子孫剿絕，為天下笑。

translations.literal: He died by another's hand, his descendants were exterminated, and he became the laughingstock of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He died at another man's hands, his line was wiped out, and he became a laughingstock throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝好悅至言，時有魏徵、王珪、虞世南、李大亮、岑文本、劉洎、馬周、褚遂良、杜正倫、高季輔，鹹以切諫，引居要職。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong delighted in the utmost words of truth; at that time Wei Zheng, Wang Gui, Yu Shinan, Li Daliang, Cen Wende, Liu Ji, Ma Zhou, Chu Suiliang, Du Zhenglun, and Gao Jifu all remonstrated sharply and were promoted to key posts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong loved to hear the plainest truth; in his day Wei Zheng, Wang Gui, Yu Shinan, Li Daliang, Cen Wende, Liu Ji, Ma Zhou, Chu Suiliang, Du Zhenglun, and Gao Jifu all offered sharp remonstrance and were placed in important posts.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂宰相曰：「自知者為難。

translations.literal: He once told his chief ministers: "Knowing oneself is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his chief ministers, "It is hard to know oneself."

sentences.zh: 如文人巧工，自謂己長，若使達者、大匠詆訶商略，則蕪辭拙跡見矣。

translations.literal: Like a literary craftsman who deems his own skill superior—if enlightened masters and great artisans criticize and appraise, his crude words and clumsy traces would be exposed.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a clever writer who thinks himself accomplished: let a master critic examine his work, and his clumsy phrasing and poor craftsmanship will be exposed at once.

sentences.zh: 天下萬機，一人聽斷，雖甚憂勞，不能盡善。

translations.literal: The myriad affairs of the realm, decided by one man's hearing and judgment—even with great worry and labor, one cannot get everything right.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad affairs of the empire are decided by one man's judgment; no matter how hard he works, he cannot get everything right.

sentences.zh: 今魏徵隨事諫正，多中朕失，如明鑒照形，美惡畢見。

translations.literal: Now Wei Zheng remonstrates and corrects on each matter, often hitting my faults—like a bright mirror reflecting a form, good and bad are fully revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wei Zheng remonstrates with me on every matter and often hits my faults exactly, like a bright mirror showing every flaw and virtue plainly.

sentences.zh: 」當是時，有上書益於政者，皆黏寢殿之壁，坐望臥觀，雖狂瞽逆意，終不以為忤。

translations.literal: " At that time, any memorial submitted that benefited governance was pasted on the walls of the sleeping hall—sitting, gazing, lying, observing—and though wild, blind, and contrary to his intent, he never took it as offense.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, any memorial that might improve governance was pasted on the walls of the imperial sleeping quarters, where he read it sitting up or lying down; even when a submission was reckless, blind, or contrary to his wishes, he never took offense.

sentences.zh: 故外事必聞，刑戮幾措，禮義大行。

translations.literal: Therefore external affairs were necessarily heard, executions were nearly set aside, and ritual and righteousness were greatly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, affairs beyond the palace were always brought to his attention, executions nearly ceased, and ritual and righteousness flourished.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不遵此道，與聖祖繼美乎？

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not follow this path and succeed to the glorious virtue of the sacred ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty not follow that example and carry forward the glorious legacy of your sage ancestor?

sentences.zh: 夫以一人之意，綜萬方之政，明有所不燭，智有所不周，上心未諭於下，下情未達於上。

translations.literal: For with one person's intent to govern the myriad policies of all regions, brightness has what it does not illuminate and wisdom has what it does not encompass—the ruler's mind is not understood below, and the sentiments below do not reach above.
translations.idiomatic: When one man's will governs the policies of the whole realm, even the brightest mind has blind spots and even the wisest judgment has its limits; what the ruler thinks may never reach those below, and what those below feel may never reach the ruler.

sentences.zh: 伏惟以虛受人，博覽兼聽，使深者不隱，遠者不塞，所謂「辟四門、明四目」也。

translations.literal: Humbly I pray that with emptiness you receive men, broadly read and listen to all, so the deep are not hidden and the far are not blocked—what is called "opening the four gates and clarifying the four eyes."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty receive people with an open mind, read widely, and listen to all sides, so that what is deep is not concealed and what is distant is not shut out—what the ancients called "opening the four gates and making clear the four eyes."

sentences.zh: 其能直言正諫不避死亡之誅者，特加寵榮，待以不次，則失之東隅，冀得之桑榆矣。

translations.literal: Those who can speak straight and remonstrate rightly without avoiding the death penalty—specially bestow favor and glory and treat them with extraordinary promotion—then though one loses at the eastern corner, one may yet gain at the mulberry and elm [twilight].
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak plainly and remonstrate rightly without fearing death should be specially honored and promoted out of turn; then, though something is lost in the morning, it may yet be recovered at dusk.

sentences.zh: 尋以母喪去官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，自陳修史有緒，家貧不能具紙筆，願得少祿以終余功。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he stated that his history-writing had progress, his family was poor and could not supply paper and brush, and he wished to receive a modest stipend to complete his remaining work.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he reported that his work on the history had made progress but that his family was too poor to afford paper and ink, and he asked for a small stipend so he could finish what remained.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜諫議大夫，復修史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Remonstrance Grand Master, and he resumed history-writing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Remonstrance Grand Master, and he returned to writing history.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，實錄留東都，詔兢馳驛取進梓宮。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, the Veritable Record remained at the Eastern Capital; Jing was ordered to ride post-haste to fetch it and deliver it to the imperial coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong died, the Veritable Record was still at the Eastern Capital, and Jing was ordered to ride post-haste to fetch it and deliver it to the imperial coffin.

sentences.zh: 以父喪解，宰相張說用趙冬曦代之。

translations.literal: On account of his father's death he resigned; the chief minister Zhang Yue had Zhao Dongxi replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when his father died, and Chief Minister Zhang Yue had Zhao Dongxi replace him.

sentences.zh: 終喪，為太子左庶子。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, he was appointed Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，帝東封太山，道中數馳射為樂。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, the Emperor performed the eastern feng sacrifice on Mount Tai; on the road he repeatedly galloped and shot for amusement.
