translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, the emperor went east to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, and along the way he repeatedly galloped and hunted for sport.

sentences.zh: 兢諫曰：「方登岱告成，不當逐狡獸，使有垂堂之危、朽株之殆。

translations.literal: Jing remonstrated: "Just as you ascend Dai to announce completion, you should not chase crafty beasts, causing the peril of hanging over a high hall or the danger of a rotted stump.
translations.idiomatic: Jing remonstrated, "You are on your way to Mount Tai to announce the completion of your reign; you should not chase wild game and risk the old proverbial dangers of standing beneath a high eave or stumbling over a rotten stump."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，大風，詔群臣陳得失。

translations.literal: The next year, in the sixth month, there was a great wind; an edict ordered the ministers to state gains and losses [of policy].
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the sixth month, a great windstorm struck, and an edict ordered the officials to set forth what was right and wrong in current policy.

sentences.zh: 兢上疏曰：「自春以來，亢陽不雨，乃六月戊午，大風拔樹，壞居人廬舍。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial: "Since spring there has been drought without rain; then on the sixth month, wuwu day, a great wind uprooted trees and ruined people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Jing submitted a memorial saying, "Since spring there has been drought without rain; then on the wuwu day of the sixth month a great wind uprooted trees and destroyed people's homes."

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『敬德不用，厥災旱。

translations.literal: The commentary says: 'When reverent virtue is not employed, the calamity is drought.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, 'When reverent virtue is not put to use, the calamity is drought.'

sentences.zh: 上下蔽隔，庶位逾節，陰侵於陽，則旱災應』。

translations.literal: When above and below are blocked and separated, common offices exceed their bounds, and yin encroaches upon yang, then drought calamity responds.'
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and subjects are cut off from one another, lesser offices overstep their bounds, and yin encroaches upon yang, drought follows.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『政悖德隱，厥風發屋壞木。

translations.literal: It also says: 'When governance is perverse and virtue is hidden, the calamity is wind that tears off roofs and breaks trees.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'When government turns perverse and virtue is concealed, the calamity is wind that tears off roofs and breaks trees.'

sentences.zh: 』風，陰類，大臣之象。

translations.literal: ' Wind belongs to the yin category and is the emblem of great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wind belongs to the yin category and symbolizes great ministers.

sentences.zh: 恐陛下左右有奸臣擅權，懷謀上之心。

translations.literal: I fear that by Your Majesty's side are treacherous ministers monopolizing power who harbor a heart to plot against the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that treacherous ministers by Your Majesty's side have seized power and harbor designs against the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣聞百王之失，皆由權移於下，故曰：『人主與人權，猶倒持太阿，授之以柄。

translations.literal: I have heard that the faults of the hundred kings all stem from authority shifting below; therefore it is said: 'A lord of men who gives men power is like holding the Tai'e sword inverted and handing them the hilt.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the failures of kings through the ages all come from power slipping down to others; hence the saying, 'When a ruler gives others his authority, it is like holding the sword Tai'e by the blade and handing them the hilt.'

sentences.zh: 』夫天降災異，欲人主感悟，願深察天變，杜絕其萌。

translations.literal: ' Heaven sends calamities and portents wanting the lord of men to awaken and perceive; I pray you deeply examine Heaven's changes and cut off their sprouting.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends omens and disasters so that the ruler may awaken; I pray Your Majesty examine these heavenly warnings closely and cut off evil at its root.

sentences.zh: 且陛下承天後、和帝之亂，府庫未充，冗員尚繁，戶口流散，法出多門，賕謁大行，趨競彌廣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty succeeded the turmoil of Empress Wu and Emperor He—the treasuries are not filled, redundant officials are still numerous, registered households have scattered, laws issue from many gates, bribery and petitioning flourish greatly, and scrambling for advancement grows ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty took the throne amid the turmoil left by Empress Wu and Emperor He: the treasuries remain empty, redundant officials are still numerous, households have scattered, laws issue from too many sources, bribery and favor-seeking run rampant, and the scramble for advancement grows ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 此弊未革，實陛下庶政之闕也，臣不勝惓惓。

translations.literal: These abuses not yet reformed are truly a shortfall in Your Majesty's myriad policies; I cannot restrain my earnest anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: That these abuses remain unreformed is truly a flaw in Your Majesty's governance, and I cannot keep from pressing my earnest concern upon you.

sentences.zh: 願斥屏群小，不為慢遊，出不禦之女，減不急之馬，明選舉，慎刑罰，杜僥幸，存至公，雖有旱風之變，不足累聖德矣。

translations.literal: I pray you banish the petty crowd, do not indulge in idle roaming, release women not needed for the inner palace, reduce horses not urgently needed, clarify selection and promotion, be cautious in punishments, block opportunism, preserve utmost fairness—then though there be drought and wind anomalies, they would not impair your sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty drive away petty men, refrain from idle roaming, release palace women who are not needed, reduce horses kept without urgent need, make selection and promotion transparent, punish with care, shut the door to opportunism, and preserve perfect fairness; then even drought and violent winds would not tarnish your sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 始，兢在長安、景龍間任史事，時武三思、張易之等監領，阿貴朋佞，釀澤浮辭，事多不實。

translations.literal: At first, during his service in history in Chang'an in the Jinglong era, Wu Sansi, Zhang Yizhi, and others supervised; they flattered the powerful, befriended sycophants, brewed muddy verbose rhetoric, and matters were mostly untrue.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while Jing was handling historiography in Chang'an during the Jinglong era, Wu Sansi, Zhang Yizhi, and others supervised the work; they fawned on the powerful, gathered flatterers around them, and produced slick, inflated prose, so that much of what was written was untrue.

sentences.zh: 兢不得誌，私撰《唐書》、《唐春秋》，未就。

translations.literal: Jing could not fulfill his intent and privately compiled The Book of Tang and Annals of Tang, but they were unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to do the work as he wished, Jing privately drafted a Book of Tang and Annals of Tang, but neither was completed.

sentences.zh: 至是，丐官筆劄，冀得成書。

translations.literal: At this point he begged for official paper and writing materials, hoping to complete the book.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he asked for official paper and writing supplies, hoping to finish the book.

sentences.zh: 詔兢就集賢院論次。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jing to go to the Hall of Assembled Worthies to organize and compile.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jing to go to the Hall of Assembled Worthies to organize and compile the history.

sentences.zh: 時張說罷宰相，在家修史。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yue had been dismissed as chief minister and was compiling history at home.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yue had left the chief ministership and was compiling history at home.

sentences.zh: 大臣奏國史不容在外，詔兢等赴館撰錄。

translations.literal: Ministers memorialized that the national history could not remain outside [the official archive]; an edict ordered Jing and others to go to the academy to compile and record.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers memorialized that the national history could not be kept outside the official archive, and an edict ordered Jing and the others to go to the academy to compile it.

sentences.zh: 進封長垣縣男。

translations.literal: He was promoted in enfeoffment to Baron of Changyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，坐書事不當，貶荊州司馬，以史草自隨。

translations.literal: After a long while, for writing matters improperly he was demoted to military administrator of Jingzhou, taking his history drafts with him.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was demoted to military administrator of Jingzhou for improper entries in the history, and he took his draft manuscripts with him.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩領國史，奏遣使者就兢取書，得六十餘篇。

translations.literal: Xiao Song supervised the national history and memorialized to send an envoy to Jing to fetch his writings; more than sixty chapters were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Song took charge of the national history, he memorialized that an envoy be sent to Jing to collect his manuscripts, and more than sixty chapters were recovered.

sentences.zh: 累遷洪州刺史，坐累下除舒州。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became prefect of Hongzhou; on accumulated offenses he was reduced and made prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to prefect of Hongzhou, but after accumulated offenses was demoted to prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，入為恒王傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he entered [court] as tutor to the Prince of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he entered court as tutor to the Prince of Heng.

sentences.zh: 雖年老衰僂甚，意猶願還史職。

translations.literal: Though old and very bent with age, in mind he still wished to return to historiographic duties.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had grown very old and was badly stooped, he still hoped in his heart to return to historiography.

sentences.zh: 李林甫嫌其衰，不用。

translations.literal: Li Linfu, disliking his decrepitude, did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu, disliking his aged infirmity, would not use him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 兢敘事簡核，號良史。

translations.literal: Jing narrated events concisely and substantively, and was called a fine historian.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wrote history in a concise and exact style and was acclaimed as a fine historian.

sentences.zh: 晚節稍疏牾。

translations.literal: In his later years he was slightly inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he became somewhat inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 時人病其太簡。

translations.literal: People of the time found fault with his being too concise.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries criticized him for being too terse.

sentences.zh: 初與劉子玄撰定《武后實錄》，敘張昌宗誘張說誣證魏元忠事，頗言「說已然可，賴宋璟等邀勵苦切，故轉禍為忠，不然，皇嗣且殆。

translations.literal: At first, together with Liu Zixuan he compiled the Veritable Record of Empress Wu, narrating how Zhang Changzong induced Zhang Yue to give false testimony against Wei Yuanzhong; it says in effect that Zhang Yue had already assented, but thanks to Song Jing and others urgently exhorting him with bitter earnestness he turned disaster into loyalty—otherwise the imperial heir would have been endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, together with Liu Zixuan he compiled the Veritable Record of Empress Wu, recounting how Zhang Changzong induced Zhang Yue to give false testimony against Wei Yuanzhong; the account states that Zhang Yue had already gone along, but that Song Jing and others urgently pressed him with fierce earnestness until he turned treachery into loyalty—otherwise the heir apparent would have been placed in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 」後說為相，讀之，心不善，知兢所為，即從容謬謂曰：「劉生書魏齊公事，不少假借，奈何？

translations.literal: Later, when Yue became chief minister and read it, he was displeased; knowing Jing was responsible, he casually and falsely said to him: "Master Liu wrote Duke Wei's affairs with little forbearance—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Yue became chief minister and read the passage, he was displeased; knowing Jing had written it, he casually and falsely remarked, "Master Liu wrote about Duke Wei's affair without much lenience—what can be done about that?"

sentences.zh: 」兢曰：「子玄已亡，不可受誣地下。

translations.literal: " Jing said: "Master Zixuan is already dead; he cannot be slandered in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Jing replied, "Master Zixuan is already dead and cannot be falsely accused in the world below.

sentences.zh: 兢實書之，其草故在。

translations.literal: It was I, Jing, who actually wrote it; the draft is still there.
translations.idiomatic: I, Jing, was the one who actually wrote it, and the draft is still in my possession.

sentences.zh: 」聞者嘆其直。

translations.literal: " Those who heard exclaimed at his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard the exchange admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 說屢以情蘄改，辭曰：「徇公之情，何名實錄？

translations.literal: Yue repeatedly appealed emotionally for changes; he replied: "Indulging private sentiment—what would that be called a veritable record?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue repeatedly pleaded with him to revise the account, but Jing refused, saying, "If I indulged private feeling, how could the work be called a veritable record?"

sentences.zh: 」卒不改。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not change it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not change a word.

sentences.zh: 世謂今董狐云。

translations.literal: The age called him the modern Dong Hu.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him the Dong Hu of his age.

sentences.zh: 韋述韋述，弘機曾孫。

translations.literal: Wei Shu—Wei Shu was a great-grandson of Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu was a great-grandson of Wei Hongji.

sentences.zh: 家廚書二千卷，述為兒時，誦憶略遍。

translations.literal: The family kitchen had two thousand volumes of books; as a child Shu could recite and recall nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: There were two thousand volumes of books in the family kitchen, and as a boy Shu could recite and recall nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 父景駿，景龍中為肥鄉令，述從到官。

translations.literal: His father Jingjun, during Jinglong, served as magistrate of Feixiang; Shu followed him to the post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingjun served as magistrate of Feixiang during the Jinglong era, and Shu accompanied him to his post.

sentences.zh: 元行沖，景駿姑子也，為時儒宗，常載書數車自隨。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingchong, Jingjun's nephew by marriage, was the great Confucian of the age and often carried several cartloads of books wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingchong, Jingjun's nephew by marriage, was the leading Confucian scholar of the day and always traveled with several cartloads of books.

sentences.zh: 述入其室觀書，不知寢食，行沖異之，試與語前世事，孰復詳諦，如指掌然。

translations.literal: Shu entered his room to view books, forgetting sleep and food; Xingchong marveled at him, tested him with talk of affairs of previous ages, and his replies were detailed and precise, as clear as the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu would enter his study to read and forget to eat or sleep; Xingchong was astonished by him and tested him with questions about past events, and Shu's answers were so detailed and precise that they seemed as clear as the lines on his palm.

sentences.zh: 使屬文，受紙輒就。

translations.literal: He had him compose a piece; given paper he immediately set to it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked him to compose a piece, and as soon as paper was placed before him Shu wrote it at once.

sentences.zh: 行沖曰：「外家之寶也。

translations.literal: Xingchong said: "He is a treasure of the maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong said, "He is a treasure of our wife's family.

sentences.zh: 」舉進士，時述方少，儀質陋侻，考功員外郎宋之問曰：「童子何業？

translations.literal: " He passed the jinshi examination; Shu was still young, his appearance coarse and unassuming; Examining Affairs Vice Director Song Zhiwen asked: "Young man, what is your specialty?
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination while still very young; his appearance was plain and unassuming. Song Zhiwen, Vice Director of Examining Affairs, asked him, "Young man, what is your field of study?

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「性嗜書，所撰《唐春秋》三十篇，恨未畢，它唯命。

translations.literal: " Shu said: "By nature I love books. I have composed thirty chapters of Annals of Tang, regretting they are not finished; otherwise whatever you command.
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "By nature I love books. I have written thirty chapters of Annals of Tang, though I regret they are not yet complete; beyond that, I am at your command.

sentences.zh: 」之問曰：「本求茂才，乃得遷、固。

translations.literal: " Zhiwen said: "I sought outstanding talent and instead got Sima Qian and Ban Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen said, "I was looking for an outstanding candidate and instead found Sima Qian and Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 」遂上第。

translations.literal: " He then placed at the top of the list.
translations.idiomatic: He then ranked Shu at the top of the list.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為櫟陽尉。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he served as marshal of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he served as marshal of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 秘書監馬懷素奏述與諸儒即秘書續《七志》，五年而成。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Ma Huaisu memorialized that Shu, together with various Confucian scholars at the secretariat, should continue the Seven Records; it was completed in five years.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Ma Huaisu memorialized that Shu, together with various scholars at the Secretariat, should continue the Seven Records; the work was completed in five years.

sentences.zh: 述好譜學，見柳沖所撰《姓族系錄》，每私寫懷之，還舍則又繕錄，故於百氏源派為詳，乃更撰《開元譜》二十篇。

translations.literal: Shu loved genealogy; seeing Liu Chong's Genealogical Record of Clans, he would privately copy and carry it in his bosom, and back at home he would copy it again, so he was detailed on the sources and branches of the hundred clans; he therefore further composed twenty chapters of Kaiyuan Genealogies.
translations.idiomatic: Shu loved the study of genealogies; whenever he saw Liu Chong's Genealogical Record of Clans he would secretly copy it and carry the copy on his person, then copy it again at home, so that he became thoroughly versed in the origins and branches of the hundred clans and went on to compose twenty chapters of Kaiyuan Genealogies.

sentences.zh: 累除右補闕。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he was appointed Right Supplementation Omissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he was appointed Right Supplementation Omissioner.

sentences.zh: 張說既領集賢院，薦述為直學士，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: After Zhang Yue took charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, he recommended Shu as a direct academician, and Shu was transferred to Diarist of the Imperial Bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Yue was put in charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, he recommended Shu as a direct academician, and Shu was promoted to diarist of the imperial bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 從封太山，奏《東封記》，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor on the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, submitted the Record of the Eastern Feng, and received an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai for the feng sacrifice, submitted a Record of the Eastern Feng, and received an imperial edict commending his work.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔修《六典》，徐堅構意歲餘，嘆曰：「吾更修七書，而《六典》歷年未有所適。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered the compilation of the Six Statutes; Xu Jian conceived the plan for more than a year and sighed, saying, "I have also revised the Seven Histories, yet after years the Six Statutes still have not taken proper shape.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when an edict ordered the compilation of the Six Statutes, Xu Jian worked out the plan for more than a year and finally sighed, "I have already revised the Seven Histories, yet after all these years the Six Statutes still have not come together."

sentences.zh: 」及蕭嵩引述撰定，述始摹周六官領其屬，事歸於職，規制遂定。

translations.literal: " When Xiao Song brought Shu in to draft and finalize it, Shu first modeled the Zhou system of six offices each overseeing its subordinates, with affairs assigned to proper duties, and the regulations were then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Song brought Shu in to draft and finalize the work, Shu modeled it on the Zhou system of six offices each overseeing its subordinates, with every affair assigned to the proper office, and the regulations were at last settled.

sentences.zh: 初，令狐德棻、吳兢等撰武德以來國史，皆不能成。

translations.literal: At first, Linghu Defen, Wu Jing, and others had compiled the national history from the Wude era onward, but none of them could bring it to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Linghu Defen, Wu Jing, and others had tried to compile the national history from the Wude reign onward, but none succeeded in finishing it.

sentences.zh: 述因二家參以後事，遂分紀、傳，又為例一篇。

translations.literal: Shu drew on the work of both houses and added later events, then divided it into annals and biographies and also wrote one chapter of precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Shu drew on the work of both earlier compilers, added later events, divided the history into annals and biographies, and also wrote a chapter of editorial precedents.

sentences.zh: 嵩欲蚤就，復奏起居舍人賈登、著作佐郎李銳助述紬績。

translations.literal: Xiao wished to finish quickly and again memorialized that Diarist Jia Deng and Assistant Compiler Li Rui should assist Shu in the editorial compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting to finish quickly, Xiao again memorialized that Diarist Jia Deng and Assistant Compiler Li Rui should help Shu with the editorial work.

sentences.zh: 逮成，文約事詳，蕭穎士以為譙周、陳壽之流。

translations.literal: When it was completed, the text was concise and the events detailed; Xiao Yingshi considered Shu the equal of Qiao Zhou and Chen Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the prose was concise and the events fully detailed; Xiao Yingshi ranked Shu with Qiao Zhou and Chen Shou.

sentences.zh: 改國子司業，充集賢學士，累遷工部侍郎，封方城縣侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, appointed academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Works, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Directorate of Education and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, promoted in succession to vice minister of works, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 述典掌圖書，余四十年，任史官二十年，淡榮利，為人純厚長者，當世宗之。

translations.literal: Shu had charge of the library collections for more than forty years and served as a historiographer for twenty; he cared little for glory and profit, was by nature pure, generous, and elder-like, and his age honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu oversaw the imperial library for more than forty years and served as a historiographer for twenty. Indifferent to rank and profit, he was by nature upright, generous, and worthy of respect, and men of his time held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 接士無貴賤與均。

translations.literal: In receiving scholars he made no distinction between high and low.
translations.idiomatic: In receiving scholars he treated the high and the low alike.

sentences.zh: 蓄書二萬卷，皆手校定，黃墨精謹，內秘書不逮也。

translations.literal: He amassed twenty thousand scrolls of books, all collated by his own hand with yellow and black ink in meticulous care, which even the inner secretariat could not match.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed twenty thousand scrolls of books, every one collated by his own hand in careful yellow and black ink—work the inner secretariat itself could not equal.

sentences.zh: 古草隸帖、秘書、古器圖譜無不備。

translations.literal: Ancient cursive and clerical copybooks, secretarial documents, and illustrated catalogues of antiquities—nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient cursive and clerical copybooks, secretarial documents, and illustrated catalogues of antiquities—he had them all.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，剽失皆盡，述獨抱國史藏南山。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, everything looted was lost; Shu alone clutched the national history and hid it in the Southern Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, everything that could be looted was lost; Shu alone clutched the national history to him and hid it in the Southern Mountains.

sentences.zh: 身陷賊，汙偽官。

translations.literal: He fell into the rebels' hands and was stained by a false office.
translations.idiomatic: He fell into rebel hands and accepted a post under the puppet regime.

sentences.zh: 賊平，流渝州，為刺史薛舒所困，不食死。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, he was exiled to Yuzhou, harassed by Prefect Xue Shu, and died by refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was exiled to Yuzhou, where Prefect Xue Shu harassed him until he died by refusing food.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，甥蕭直為李光弼判官，詣闕奏事稱旨。

translations.literal: In the early Guangde era, his nephew Xiao Zhi served as aide to Li Guangbi; he went to court to report affairs and pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangde era his nephew Xiao Zhi, serving as aide to Li Guangbi, went to court to report on affairs and pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 因理述「蒼卒奔逼，能存國史，賊平，盡送史官於休烈，以功補過，宜蒙恩宥。

translations.literal: Thereupon he argued on Shu's behalf: "In the sudden rush of flight he was still able to preserve the national history; when the rebels were suppressed he sent it all to the historiographer Yu Xiulie. Merit should offset fault, and he ought to receive imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he argued on Shu's behalf: "In the sudden chaos of flight Shu was still able to preserve the national history; when the rebels were suppressed he sent it all to the historiographer Yu Xiulie. His merit should offset his fault, and he deserves imperial clemency.

sentences.zh: 」有詔贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued posthumously appointing him Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued posthumously appointing him Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 韋氏之顯者，孝友、詞學則承慶、嗣立，邃音樂有萬石，達禮儀則叔夏，史才博識有述。

translations.literal: Among the distinguished of the Wei clan: in filial piety and friendship and in literary learning there were Chengqing and Siliz; in deep mastery of music there was Wanshi; in mastery of ritual there was Shuxia; in historiographical talent and broad learning there was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Among the distinguished members of the Wei clan, Chengqing and Siliz excelled in filial piety, friendship, and literary learning; Wanshi in deep mastery of music; Shuxia in ritual; and Shu in historiographical talent and broad learning.

sentences.zh: 所著書二百餘篇行於時。

translations.literal: The more than two hundred works he wrote circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred works he wrote circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 弟逌、迪，學業亦亞述。

translations.literal: His younger brothers You and Di were also slightly below Shu in scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers You and Di were only slightly less accomplished in scholarship than Shu.

sentences.zh: 與逌對為學士，與迪並禮官，搢紳高之。

translations.literal: He and You served together as academicians; he and Di served together as ritual officials—the gentry held them in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He and You served together as academicians, and he and Di served together as ritual officials; the gentry held them in high regard.

sentences.zh: 時趙冬曦兄弟亦各有名。

translations.literal: At the time the brothers of Zhao Dongxi also each had a name.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the brothers of Zhao Dongxi were also each celebrated in their own right.

sentences.zh: 張說嘗曰「韋、趙兄弟，人之杞梓」云。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue once said, "The Wei and Zhao brothers are the fine timber among men."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue once said, "The Wei and Zhao brothers are the finest timber among men."

sentences.zh: 蔣乂蔣乂，字德源，常州義興人，徙家河南。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi—Jiang Yi, courtesy name Deyuan, was a native of Yixing in Changzhou and moved his household to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi, courtesy name Deyuan, was a native of Yixing in Changzhou and later moved his household to Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖瑰，開元中弘文館學士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was an academician of the Hongwen Hall in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui was an academician of the Hongwen Hall during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 父將明，天寶末，辟河中使府。

translations.literal: His father Jiangming, in the late Tianbao era, was recruited into the Hezhong military commissioner’s staff.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiangming, in the late Tianbao era, was recruited onto the staff of the Hezhong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，以計佐其帥，全並、潞等州。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he used stratagems to assist the commander and preserved Bing and Lu among other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he used stratagems to assist the commander and preserved Bing and Lu among other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 兩京陷，被拘，乃陽狂以免。

translations.literal: When the two capitals fell, he was detained, and so feigned madness to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals fell he was detained, and feigned madness to escape harm.

sentences.zh: 虢王巨引致幕府，歷侍御史，擢左司郎中、國子司業、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Prince Guo Ju brought him into his staff; he served successively as investigating censor and was promoted to Left Department Director, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guo Ju brought him onto his staff; he served as investigating censor and was promoted to left department director, vice director of the Directorate of Education, and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乂性銳敏，七歲時，見庾信《哀江南賦》，再讀輒誦。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature sharp and quick; at age seven, when he saw Yu Xin's Lament for the South, after reading it twice he could recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was sharp and quick by nature; at seven, when he saw Yu Xin's Lament for the South, he could recite it after reading it only twice.

sentences.zh: 外祖吳兢位史官，乂幼從外家學，得其書，博覽強記。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Wu Jing held the post of historiographer; Yi studied from childhood in his mother's family, obtained his books, and read widely with a strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Wu Jing served as historiographer; Yi studied from childhood in his mother's family, gained access to his books, and read widely with a formidable memory.

sentences.zh: 逮冠，該綜群籍，有史才，司徒楊綰尤稱之。

translations.literal: By the time he came of age he had mastered the corpus of books, possessed historiographical talent, and Minister of Works Yang Guan especially praised him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age he had mastered the corpus of books and showed historiographical talent; Minister of Works Yang Guan especially praised him.

sentences.zh: 將明在集賢，值兵興，圖籍殽舛，白宰相請引乂入院，助力整比。

translations.literal: Jiangming was at the Hall of Assembled Worthies; when war broke out the library collections were disordered and confused, and he told the chief minister to bring Yi into the academy to help sort and collate them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangming was serving at the Hall of Assembled Worthies; when war broke out the library collections were thrown into disorder, and he asked the chief minister to bring Yi into the academy to help sort and collate them.

sentences.zh: 宰相張鎰亦奇之，署集賢小職。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yi also considered him remarkable and appointed him to a minor post in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yi also considered him remarkable and gave him a minor post in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乂料次逾年，各以部分，得善書二萬卷。

translations.literal: Yi catalogued them for more than a year, assigning each to its proper category, and obtained twenty thousand scrolls of fine books.
translations.idiomatic: Yi spent more than a year cataloguing them by category and recovered twenty thousand scrolls of fine books.

sentences.zh: 再遷王屋尉，充太常禮院修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to magistrate of Wangwu and appointed compiler for the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to magistrate of Wangwu and appointed a compiler in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，擢右拾遺、史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Zhenyuan era he was promoted to Right Reminder and historiographer of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Zhenyuan era he was promoted to right reminder and historiographer of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 德宗重其職，先召見延英，乃命之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong valued the post; he first summoned Yi to the Yanying Hall for an audience and only then issued the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong valued the post highly; he first summoned Yi to the Yanying Hall for an audience and only then issued the appointment.

sentences.zh: 張孝忠子茂宗尚義章公主，母亡，遺言丐成禮。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaozhong's son Maozong was betrothed to Princess Yizhang; when his mother died, her dying wish was to beg that the marriage rites be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong's son Maozong was betrothed to Princess Yizhang; when his mother died, her dying wish was that the marriage rites still be completed.

sentences.zh: 帝念孝忠功，即日召為左衛將軍，許主下降。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of Xiaozhong's merit, that same day summoned Maozong to be General of the Left Guard and permitted the princess to descend in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Xiaozhong's service, the emperor that same day summoned Maozong to be General of the Left Guard and permitted the princess to marry him.

sentences.zh: 乂上疏，以為：「墨缞禮本緣金革，未有奪喪尚主者。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial, arguing: "The rites of black hemp mourning originally arise from military campaigns; there has never been one who, while seizing mourning, still married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial arguing: "The rites of black hemp mourning originally arise from military campaigns; there has never been a case of marrying a princess while cutting short mourning."

sentences.zh: 繆盩典禮，違人情，不可為法。

translations.literal: To grossly confuse the canonical rites, violate human feeling, and make this a precedent is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To grossly confuse the canonical rites, violate human feeling, and set this as a precedent is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 」帝令中使者諭茂宗之母之請，乂意殊堅。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent a palace envoy to explain the request of Maozong's mother, but Yi's resolve was especially firm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to explain Maozong's mother's request, but Yi remained especially firm.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿所言，古禮也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you say is the ancient rite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you say follows the ancient rite.

sentences.zh: 今俗借吉而婚不為少。

translations.literal: In present custom, borrowing an auspicious day for marriage is not rare.
translations.idiomatic: In present custom, borrowing an auspicious day for marriage is hardly uncommon.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「俚室窮人子，旁無至親，乃有借吉以嫁，不聞男冒兇而娶。

translations.literal: " He replied, "In common households, when a poor man's daughter has no close kin nearby, there are cases of borrowing an auspicious day to marry her off; one never hears of a man marrying while still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In common households, when a poor man's daughter has no close kin nearby, there are cases of borrowing an auspicious day to marry her off—but one never hears of a man marrying while still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 陛下建中詔書，郡、縣主當婚，皆使有司循典故，毋用俗儀。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Jianzhong edict stated that when commandery and county princesses marry, the relevant offices should follow canonical precedents and not use popular custom.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's Jianzhong edict stated that when commandery and county princesses marry, the relevant offices should follow canonical precedents and not resort to popular custom.

sentences.zh: 公主春秋少，待年不為晚，請茂宗如禮便。

translations.literal: The princess is still young; waiting until she comes of age would not be late—please let Maozong observe the rites properly.
translations.idiomatic: The princess is still young; waiting until she comes of age would not be too late—please let Maozong observe the rites properly.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「更思之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I will think further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I will think further about this.

sentences.zh: 」會太常博士韋彤、裴堪諫曰：「婚禮，主人几筵聽命，稱事立文，謂之嘉，所以承宗廟，繼後嗣也。

translations.literal: " At that time the Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tong and Pei Kan remonstrated, saying, "In the marriage rites the host sets out the spirit tablet and mat to receive commands, establishes the text according to the occasion, and calls it auspicious—this is to carry on the ancestral temple and continue the line.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tong and Pei Kan remonstrated, saying, "In the marriage rites the host sets out the spirit tablet and mat to receive commands and establishes the text according to the occasion—this is called auspicious, for it carries on the ancestral temple and continues the line.

sentences.zh: 喪禮，創巨者日久，痛甚者愈遲，二十五月而畢，謂之兇，所以送死報終，示有節也。

translations.literal: In mourning rites, the greater the wound the longer the time, the deeper the grief the slower the recovery; after twenty-five months it is complete—this is called mourning, for it sends off the dead and completes the end, showing that there are limits.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning rites, the greater the wound the longer the time, the deeper the grief the slower the recovery; after twenty-five months it is complete—this is called mourning, for it sends off the dead and completes the rites, showing that there are limits.

sentences.zh: 故夫義婦聽，父慈子孝。

translations.literal: Thus husbands are righteous and wives compliant, fathers kind and sons filial.
translations.idiomatic: Thus husbands are righteous and wives compliant, fathers kind and sons filial.

sentences.zh: 昔魯侯改服，晉襄墨缞，緣金革事則有權變。

translations.literal: Formerly the Marquis of Lu changed his garb and Duke Xiang of Jin wore black hemp mourning—all because of military campaigns there were expedient changes.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Marquis of Lu changed his garb and Duke Xiang of Jin wore black hemp mourning—because military campaigns sometimes require expedient changes.

sentences.zh: 安有釋缞服，衣冕裳，去堊室，行親迎，以兇瀆嘉，為朝廷爽法？

translations.literal: How can one cast off hemp mourning, put on court robes and skirts, leave the white-washed mourning chamber, and go to meet the bride in person—using mourning to profane what is auspicious and making the court violate its own law?
translations.idiomatic: How can one cast off hemp mourning, put on court robes, leave the white-washed mourning chamber, and go to meet the bride in person—using mourning to profane what is auspicious and making the court violate its own law?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝迂其言，促行前詔，然心嘉乂有守。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor circumvented their words and hurried forward the earlier edict, yet in his heart he admired Yi's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor set their words aside and hurried forward the earlier edict, yet in his heart he admired Yi's integrity.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷起居舍人，轉司勛員外，皆兼史任。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to diarist of the imperial bedchamber and then to outer-section director of the Ministry of Personnel, in both cases concurrently holding historiographical duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to diarist of the imperial bedchamber and then to outer-section director of the Ministry of Personnel, in both cases while retaining his historiographical duties.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗登淩煙閣，視左壁頹剝，題文漫缺，行才數字，命錄以問宰相，無能知者。

translations.literal: The emperor once ascended the Lingyan Pavilion; seeing the left wall crumbling and peeling, the inscribed text blurred and missing with only a few characters in each line, he ordered it copied and shown to the chief ministers, but none could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ascended the Lingyan Pavilion and saw the left wall crumbling and peeling, the inscribed text blurred and missing with only a few characters per line; he ordered it copied and shown to the chief ministers, but none could identify it.

sentences.zh: 遽召乂至，答曰：「此聖歷中侍臣圖贊。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Yi, who answered, "This is the portrait eulogy of attendant ministers from the Shengli era.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately summoned Yi, who answered, "This is the portrait eulogy of attendant ministers from the Shengli era.

sentences.zh: 」帝前口以誦補，不失一字。

translations.literal: " Before the emperor he recited from memory to fill in the missing parts, not missing a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor he recited from memory to fill in the missing parts, not missing a single character.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「雖虞世南默寫《列女傳》，不是過。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said, "Even Yu Shinan's silent transcription of the Biographies of Exemplary Women would not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "Even Yu Shinan's silent transcription of the Biographies of Exemplary Women would not surpass this.

sentences.zh: 」會詔問神策軍建置本末，中書討求不獲，時集賢學士甚眾，悉亡以對。

translations.literal: " Soon an edict asked about the origins and development of the Shence Army; the Secretariat searched but could not find the answer, and though the academicians of the Hall of Assembled Worthies were many, none could reply.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict asked about the origins and development of the Shence Army; the Secretariat searched but could not find the answer, and though many academicians of the Hall of Assembled Worthies were present, none could reply.

sentences.zh: 乃訪乂，乂條據甚詳。

translations.literal: They then consulted Yi, and Yi set forth the evidence in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: They then consulted Yi, and he set forth the evidence in great detail.

sentences.zh: 宰相高郢、鄭珣瑜嘆曰：「集賢有人哉！

translations.literal: Chief ministers Gao Yi and Zheng Xunyu exclaimed, "The Hall of Assembled Worthies has its man!
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Gao Yi and Zheng Xunyu exclaimed, "The Hall of Assembled Worthies has its man!

sentences.zh: 」明日，詔兼判集賢院事。

translations.literal: " The next day an edict appointed him concurrently to administer the affairs of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict appointed him concurrently to administer the affairs of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 父子為學士，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Father and son both served as academicians—a glory for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both served as academicians—a glory for scholars.

sentences.zh: 順宗既葬，議祧廟，有司以中宗中興之君，當百代不遷。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shunzong was buried, they debated shifting the ancestral temples; the relevant offices held that Emperor Zhongzong was a restoration emperor and should never be moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shunzong was buried, the court debated shifting the ancestral temples; the relevant offices held that Emperor Zhongzong was a restoration emperor whose tablet should never be moved for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 宰相問乂，乂曰：「中宗即位，春秋已壯，而母后篡奪以移神器，賴張柬之等國祚再復，蓋曰反正，不得為中興。

translations.literal: The chief ministers asked Yi, and Yi said, "When Zhongzong took the throne he was already a grown man, yet the empress dowager usurped power and shifted the imperial regalia; relying on Zhang Jianzhi and others the dynastic line was restored—this is called setting right what was wrong, not a true restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked Yi, and he said, "When Zhongzong took the throne he was already a grown man, yet the empress dowager usurped power and seized the imperial regalia; only through Zhang Jianzhi and others was the dynastic line restored—this is called setting right what was wrong, not a true restoration.

sentences.zh: 凡非我失之，自我復之，為中興，漢光武、晉元是也。

translations.literal: Whenever what was lost was not by our own doing and what was restored was by our own doing, that is a restoration—Emperor Guangwu of Han and Emperor Yuan of Jin are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever what was lost was not by our own doing and what was restored was by our own doing, that is a true restoration—Emperor Guangwu of Han and Emperor Yuan of Jin are examples.

sentences.zh: 自我失之，因人復之，晉孝惠、孝安是也。

translations.literal: What was lost by our own doing and restored through others—Emperors Xiaohui and Xiao'an of Jin are examples.
translations.idiomatic: What was lost by our own doing and restored through others—Emperors Xiaohui and Xiao'an of Jin are examples.

sentences.zh: 今中宗與惠、安二帝同，不可為不遷主。

translations.literal: Now Zhongzong is the same as the two emperors Hui and An; he cannot be treated as an emperor whose tablet is never moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong falls into the same category as Emperors Hui and An; he cannot be treated as an emperor whose tablet is never moved.

sentences.zh: 」有司疑曰：「五王有安社稷功，若遷中宗，則配饗永絕。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices doubted, saying, "The Five Princes had the merit of securing the state; if Zhongzong is moved, their joint sacrifice would be cut off forever.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices objected, saying, "The Five Princes had the merit of securing the state; if Zhongzong's tablet is moved, their joint sacrifice would be cut off forever.

sentences.zh: 」乂曰：「禘袷功臣，乃合食太廟。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "Meritorious ministers at the di and xia sacrifices jointly partake of the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Meritorious ministers at the di and xia sacrifices jointly partake of offerings in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 中宗廟雖毀，而禘祫並陳太廟，此則五王配食與初一也。

translations.literal: Although Zhongzong's temple would be removed, at the di and xia sacrifices all are displayed together in the Grand Ancestral Temple—thus the Five Princes' joint sacrifice would be the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhongzong's temple would be removed, at the di and xia sacrifices all tablets are displayed together in the Grand Ancestral Temple—thus the Five Princes' joint sacrifice would remain as before.

sentences.zh: 」由是遷廟遂定。

translations.literal: " By this the shifting of the temples was settled.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis the shifting of the temples was settled.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 與許孟容、韋貫之刪正制敕三十篇，為《開元格後敕》。

translations.literal: Together with Xu Mengrong and Wei Guanzhi he revised thirty chapters of edicts and regulations, forming the Post-Kaiyuan Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xu Mengrong and Wei Guanzhi he revised thirty chapters of edicts and regulations, producing the Post-Kaiyuan Edicts.

sentences.zh: 李锜誅，詔宗正削一房屬籍。

translations.literal: When Li Yi was executed, an edict ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan to strike one branch from the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yi was executed, an edict ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan to strike one branch from the clan register.

sentences.zh: 宰相召乂問：「一房自大功可乎？

translations.literal: The chief ministers summoned Yi and asked, "Would one branch from the great-great-grandfather's line suffice?
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers summoned Yi and asked, "Would one branch from the great-great-grandfather's line suffice?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「大功，锜之從父昆弟。

translations.literal: " He replied, "The great-great-grandfather's line would be Yi's father's cousins.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The great-great-grandfather's line would be Yi's father's cousins.

sentences.zh: 其祖神通有功，配饗於廟，雖裔孫之惡，而忘其勛，不可。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shentong had merit and received joint sacrifice in the temple; though a descendant's crime was evil, to forget his achievement would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shentong had merit and received joint sacrifice in the temple; though a descendant's crime was evil, to forget his achievement would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 」「自期可乎？

translations.literal: " "Would starting from Qi suffice?
translations.idiomatic: "Would starting from Qi suffice?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「期者锜昆弟。

translations.literal: " He said, "Qi was Yi's brother.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Qi was Yi's brother.

sentences.zh: 其父若幽死社稷，今以锜連坐，不可。

translations.literal: Their father Ruoyou died for the state; to punish him now because of Yi's guilt by association would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Ruoyou died for the state; to punish him now because of Yi's guilt by association would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 」執政然之。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers agreed.

sentences.zh: 故罪止锜及子息，無旁坐者。

translations.literal: Therefore punishment was limited to Yi and his sons; there were no collateral punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore punishment was limited to Yi and his sons; no collateral relatives were punished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改秘書少監，復兼史館修撰，與獨孤郁、韋處厚修《德宗實錄》。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and again concurrently historiographer of the History Office; together with Dugu Yu and Wei Chuhou he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice director of the Secretariat and again concurrently historiographer of the History Office; together with Dugu Yu and Wei Chuhou he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 以勞遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: For his labor he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: For his labors he was promoted to right remonstrance adviser.

sentences.zh: 裴垍罷宰相，而李吉甫惡垍，以嘗監修，故授乂太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Pei Ji was removed as chief minister and Li Jifu hated Ji, because Yi had once supervised the compilation he was given the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji was removed as chief minister and Li Jifu, who hated Ji, learned that Yi had once supervised the compilation, Yi was given the post of vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷秘書監，累封義興縣公。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and in succession was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to director of the Secretariat and in succession was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，贈禮部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites, with posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age seventy-five; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 乂在朝廷久，居史職二十年。

translations.literal: Yi had long been at court and held historiographical office for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had long served at court and held historiographical office for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 每有大政事議論，宰相未能決，必咨訪之，乂據經義或舊章以參時事，其對允切該詳。

translations.literal: Whenever great affairs of state were debated and the chief ministers could not decide, they always consulted him; Yi would draw on canonical principles or old regulations to address current affairs, and his replies were fair, apt, and comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great affairs of state were debated and the chief ministers could not decide, they always consulted him; Yi would draw on canonical principles or old regulations to address current affairs, and his replies were fair, apt, and comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 初以是被遇，終亦忤貴近，介介不至顯官。

translations.literal: At first he was favored for this, but in the end he also offended the powerful and the close, and through scrupulous integrity never reached a high office.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was favored for this, but in the end he also offended the powerful and the well-connected, and through scrupulous integrity never reached a high office.

sentences.zh: 然資質樸直，遇權臣秉政，輒數歲不遷。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was plain and upright; when powerful ministers held power, he would go years without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was plain and upright; whenever powerful ministers held sway, he would go years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏裴延齡罪惡及拒王叔文，當世高之。

translations.literal: He once memorialized against the crimes of Pei Yanling and refused Wang Shuwen; men of his time held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized against the crimes of Pei Yanling and refused Wang Shuwen; men of his time held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 結髮誌學，老而不厭，雖甚寒暑，卷不釋於前，故能通百家學，尤明前世沿革。

translations.literal: From the time he tied his hair he resolved to study, and to old age he did not weary; even in extreme cold or heat he would not put down the scroll before him, and so he mastered the learning of the hundred schools, especially the institutional changes of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he tied his hair he resolved to study, and to old age he did not weary; even in extreme cold or heat he would not put down the scroll before him, and so he mastered the learning of the hundred schools, especially the institutional changes of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 家藏書至萬五千卷。

translations.literal: The books in his household collection reached fifteen thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The books in his household collection reached fifteen thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初名武，憲宗時因進見，請曰：「陛下今日偃武修文，群臣當順承上意，請改名乂。

translations.literal: His original name was Wu; during Emperor Xianzong's reign, on an audience at court he requested, saying, "Your Majesty today halts warfare and promotes culture; the ministers ought to follow and carry out the sovereign's intent—I beg to change my name to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Wu; during Emperor Xianzong's reign, on an audience at court he requested, "Your Majesty today halts warfare and promotes culture; the ministers ought to follow and carry out the sovereign's intent—I beg to change my name to Yi.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 時討王承宗兵方罷，乂恐天子銳於武，亦因以諷。

translations.literal: At that time the campaign against Wang Chengzong had just ended; Yi feared the Son of Heaven was keen on warfare and used this as an indirect admonition as well.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the campaign against Wang Chengzong had just ended; Yi feared the emperor was eager for war and used the occasion to offer an indirect admonition as well.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝見侍御史唐武曰：「命名固多，何必曰武？

translations.literal: Another day the emperor saw the attendant censor Tang Wu and said, "There are certainly many names—why must one be called Wu?
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor saw the attendant censor Tang Wu and said, "There are certainly many names to choose from—why must one be called Wu?

sentences.zh: 乂既改之矣。

translations.literal: Yi had already changed his.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had already changed his.

sentences.zh: 」更曰慶。

translations.literal: " He changed it again to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: " He changed it again to Qing.

sentences.zh: 群臣乃知帝且厭兵云。

translations.literal: The ministers then knew the emperor was already weary of war.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then understood that the emperor had grown weary of war.

sentences.zh: 乂論撰百餘篇。

translations.literal: Yi wrote more than a hundred discursive essays.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote more than a hundred discursive essays.

sentences.zh: 五子：係、伸、偕知名，仙、佶皆位刺史。

translations.literal: Five sons: Xi, Shen, and Xie were well known; Xian and Ji both held posts as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Xi, Shen, and Xie were well known, while Xian and Ji both served as prefects.

sentences.zh: 乂子 係係善屬文，得父典實。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi's son Xi—Xi was skilled at composition and mastered his father's factual materials.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi's son Xi was skilled at literary composition and had mastered his father's store of documented facts.

sentences.zh: 大和初，授昭應尉，直史館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dahe era he was appointed Defender of Zhaoying and served on duty at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dahe era he was appointed Defender of Zhaoying and assigned to duty at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜右拾遺、史館修撰，與沈傳師、鄭澣、陳夷行、李漢參撰《憲宗實錄》。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Right Reminder and Historiography Compiler, and with Shen Chuanshi, Zheng Huan, Chen Yixing, and Li Han jointly compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Right Reminder and Historiography Compiler and, together with Shen Chuanshi, Zheng Huan, Chen Yixing, and Li Han, helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 轉右補闕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplements Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Supplements Clerk.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫被誣，文宗怒甚，係與左常侍崔玄亮涕泣苦諍，申錫得不死。

translations.literal: When Song Shenxi was falsely accused, Emperor Wenzong was greatly angered; Xi and Left Regular Attendant Cui Xuanliang wept and remonstrated strenuously, and Shenxi was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Shenxi was falsely accused, Emperor Wenzong was furious; Xi and Left Regular Attendant Cui Xuanliang wept and remonstrated bitterly, and Shenxi was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 歷膳部員外、工禮兵三部郎中，皆兼史職。

translations.literal: He successively served as Secretary in the Boards of Delicacies, Works, Rites, and War, all while holding concurrent historian posts.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as secretary in the boards of delicacies, works, rites, and war, all while retaining concurrent historian duties.

sentences.zh: 開成末，轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaicheng era he was transferred to Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaicheng era he was promoted to Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 宰相李德裕惡李漢，以係友婿，出為桂管觀察使，人安其治。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Deyu hated Li Han; because Xi was Han's friend and son-in-law, he was sent out as Military Commissioner of Guiguan Circuit, and the people were at ease under his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Deyu hated Li Han; because Xi was Han's friend and son-in-law, he was sent out as military commissioner of Guiguan Circuit, where the people lived peacefully under his rule.

sentences.zh: 復坐漢貶唐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again demoted, through Han's disgrace, to Prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again, caught up in Han's fall, to prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，召為給事中、集賢殿學士判院事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded he was summoned as Supervising Censor and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was recalled as supervising censor and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部侍郎，歷興元、鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and successively served as Military Commissioner of Xingyuan and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of personnel and successively served as military commissioner of Xingyuan and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 懿宗初，拜兵部尚書，以弟伸位丞相，懇辭，乃檢校尚書右仆射，節度山南東道，封淮陽郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yizong's reign he was appointed Minister of War; because his younger brother Shen held the chancellorship he earnestly declined, and was instead made Inspector-General of the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Military Commissioner of the Shannandong Circuit, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Yizong's reign he was appointed minister of war; because his younger brother Shen was chief minister, he earnestly declined, and was instead made inspector-general of the right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and military commissioner of Shannandong Circuit, enfeoffed as duke of Huaiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 徙東都留守，卒。

translations.literal: He was moved to eastern capital intendant and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to eastern capital intendant and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子曙，字耀之。

translations.literal: His son Shao, courtesy name Yaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao, courtesy name Yaozhi.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，由進士第署鄂嶽團練判官，除虞、工二部員外，改起居郎。

translations.literal: In the late Xiantong era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Registrar of the E'yue Defense Command; he was made Outer Department Secretary of the Boards of Revenue and Works, then changed to Attendant of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Xiantong era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of the E'yue defense command; he was then made outer department secretary of the boards of revenue and works, and later transferred to attendant of the left.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之難，曙闔門無噍類，以是絕意仕進，隱居沈痛。

translations.literal: During the Huang Chao disaster Shao's entire household was wiped out, leaving no survivors; on this account he renounced all ambition for office and lived in seclusion in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huang Chao uprising Shao's entire household was wiped out, leaving no one alive; from then on he abandoned all ambition for office and lived in seclusion, consumed by grief.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，表請為道士，許之。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhonghe era he submitted a memorial asking to become a Daoist priest; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhonghe era he submitted a memorial requesting to become a Daoist priest, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 乂子 伸伸，字大直，第進士。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi's son Shen—Shen, courtesy name Dazhi, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi's son Shen, courtesy name Dazhi, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中二年，以右補闕為史館修撰，轉駕部郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Dazhong era he served as Right Supplements Clerk and Historiography Compiler, was transferred to Director of the Imperial Transport Section, and managed imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dazhong era he served as right supplements clerk and historiography compiler, was transferred to director of the imperial transport section, and took charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 白敏中領邠寧節度，表伸自副，加右庶子。

translations.literal: When Bai Minzhong took command of the Binning Circuit he listed Shen as his deputy, adding the title of Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Minzhong took command of Binning Circuit he appointed Shen as his deputy, adding the title of right subordinate of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 入知戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice minister of the board of revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，為翰林學士，進承旨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he became Hanlin Academician and advanced to Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became a Hanlin academician and was promoted to chief academician.

sentences.zh: 十年，改兵部侍郎，判戶部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Vice Minister of War while concurrently directing the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to vice minister of war while concurrently directing the board of revenue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗雅信愛伸，每見必咨天下得失。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong trusted and favored Shen greatly; whenever he saw him he always consulted him on the gains and losses of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong trusted and favored Shen deeply; whenever they met he would consult him on the affairs of the realm and their consequences.

sentences.zh: 伸言：「比爵賞稍易，人且偷。

translations.literal: Shen said, "Recently rank and reward have been granted a little too easily; people will grow complacent.
translations.idiomatic: Shen said, "Lately ranks and rewards have been granted a little too easily; people will grow complacent.

sentences.zh: 」帝愕然曰：「偷則亂矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor started and said, "Complacency would bring disorder.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor started and said, "Complacency would bring disorder.

sentences.zh: 」伸曰：「否，非遽亂，但人有覬心，亂由是生。

translations.literal: " Shen said, "No—not immediate disorder, but once people have covetous hearts, disorder arises from that.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen said, "No—not immediate disorder, but once people harbor covetous hearts, disorder grows from that.

sentences.zh: 」帝嗟嘆，伸三起三留，曰：「它日不復獨對卿矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor sighed in admiration; Shen rose three times and was detained three times, saying, "Another day I shall no longer be granted a private audience with you.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed in admiration; Shen rose to leave three times and was detained three times, saying, "Another day I shall no longer be granted a private audience with you.

sentences.zh: 」伸不諭。

translations.literal: " Shen did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen did not understand.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Associate Director of the Chancellery with the same office title.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made associate director of the chancellery with the same office title.

sentences.zh: 逾四月，解戶部，加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than four months he was relieved of the Board of Revenue charge and promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After more than four months he was relieved of his charge over the board of revenue and promoted to vice director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 懿宗即位，兼刑部尚書，監修國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yizong took the throne he was additionally Minister of Justice and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yizong took the throne he was additionally made minister of justice and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 咸通二年，出為河中節度使、同中書門下平章事，徙宣武。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xiantong era he was sent out as Military Commissioner of Hedong with concurrent chancellorship, then transferred to Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xiantong era he was sent out as military commissioner of Hedong with concurrent chancellorship, then transferred to Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 俄以太子少保分司東都。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made the Heir Apparent's Junior Preceptor with duty at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was made junior preceptor of the heir apparent with duty at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 七年，用為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was employed as Prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷太子太傅，表乞骸骨，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he retired with his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to grand preceptor of the heir apparent and submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he retired with his original rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 乂子 偕偕以父任，歷右拾遺、史館修撰，轉補闕、主客郎中。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi's son Xie—Xie entered office through his father's position, and successively served as Right Reminder, Historiography Compiler, Supplements Clerk, and Director of the Office of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi's son Xie entered office through his father's position and successively served as right reminder, historiography compiler, supplements clerk, and director of the office of receptions.

sentences.zh: 初，柳芳作《唐歷》，大歷以後闕而不錄，宣宗詔崔龜從、韋澳、李荀、張彥遠及偕等分年撰次，盡元和以續云。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Fang had compiled the Tang Annals; after the Dali era entries were left unrecorded; Emperor Xuanzong ordered Cui Guicong, Wei Ao, Li Xun, Zhang Yanyuan, and Xie among others to arrange chronologically year by year, continuing it through the Yuanhe reign.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Fang had compiled the Tang Annals, but events after the Dali era were left unrecorded; Emperor Xuanzong ordered Cui Guicong, Wei Ao, Li Xun, Zhang Yanyuan, Xie, and others to arrange events year by year and continue the work through the Yuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大中八年，與盧耽、牛叢、王沨、盧告撰次《文宗實錄》。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong he joined Lu Dan, Niu Cong, Wang Feng, and Lu Gao in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dazhong he joined Lu Dan, Niu Cong, Wang Feng, and Lu Gao in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 蔣氏世禪儒，唯伸及系子兆能以辭章取進士第，然不為文士所多。

translations.literal: The Jiang clan for generations transmitted Confucian study; only Shen and Xi's son Zhao were able to win the jinshi through belles-lettres, yet they were not greatly favored by men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang clan had transmitted Confucian learning for generations; only Shen and Xi's son Zhao won the jinshi through literary composition, yet they were not much admired by men of letters.

sentences.zh: 三世踵修國史，世稱良筆，咸云「蔣氏日歷」，天下多藏焉。

translations.literal: Three generations in succession revised the national history; the age called them skilled pens, and all spoke of "the Jiang clan's daily chronicle"—copies were widely collected throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations in succession revised the national history; the age called them skilled historians, and people everywhere spoke of "the Jiang clan's daily chronicle"—copies were widely collected throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 柳芳柳芳，字仲敷，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, courtesy name Zhongfu, a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, courtesy name Zhongfu, was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元末，擢進士第，由永寧尉直史館。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination and, from his post as Defender of Yongning, served on duty at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination and, from his post as defender of Yongning, served on duty at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔芳與韋述綴輯吳兢所次國史，會述死，芳緒成之，興高祖，訖乾元，凡百三十篇。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong ordered Fang and Wei Shu to continue compiling the national history arranged by Wu Jing; when Shu died Fang took up the threads and completed it, from the rise of the High Founder through the Qianyuan era—in all 130 chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong ordered Fang and Wei Shu to continue compiling the national history arranged by Wu Jing; when Shu died Fang took up the work and finished it, from the rise of the High Founder through the Qianyuan era—in all 130 chapters.

sentences.zh: 敘天寶後事，棄取不倫，史官病之。

translations.literal: In narrating events after the Tianbao era he discarded and selected without consistent principle; the historians lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: In narrating events after the Tianbao era he discarded and selected material without consistent principle, and the historians deplored this.

sentences.zh: 上元中，坐事徙黔中。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan period he was demoted and exiled to Qianzhong for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan period he was demoted and exiled to Qianzhong for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後歷左金吾衛騎曹參軍、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Adjunct of the Left Golden Spear Guard and Compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Later he successively served as adjunct of the left golden spear guard and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 然芳篤誌論著，不少選忘厭。

translations.literal: Yet Fang was deeply devoted to scholarly writing and never slackened or wearied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fang was deeply devoted to scholarly writing and never slackened or grew weary.

sentences.zh: 承寇亂史籍淪缺。

translations.literal: In the wake of rebellion and disorder the historical archives were lost and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of rebellion and disorder the historical archives were lost and ruined.

sentences.zh: 芳始謫時，高力士亦貶巫州，因從力士質開元、天寶及禁中事，具識本末。

translations.literal: When Fang was first demoted, Gao Lishi was also banished to Wuzhou; he therefore sought from Lishi firsthand knowledge of the Kaiyuan, Tianbao, and inner-palace affairs and fully learned the sequence of events.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang was first demoted, Gao Lishi was also banished to Wuzhou; he therefore questioned Lishi about Kaiyuan, Tianbao, and inner-palace affairs and fully learned how events had unfolded.

sentences.zh: 時國史已送官，不可追刊，乃推衍義類，仿編年法，為《唐歷》四十篇，頗有異聞。

translations.literal: At that time the national history had already been delivered to the office and could not be revised retroactively; he therefore extended the categories of meaning, imitated the annalistic method, and wrote the Tang Annals in forty chapters, containing much material not found elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the national history had already been submitted to the office and could not be revised retroactively; he therefore extended its categories of meaning, imitated the annalistic method, and wrote the Tang Annals in forty chapters, containing much material not found elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 然不立褒貶義例，為諸儒譏訕。

translations.literal: Yet he established no standards of praise and blame; the various scholars mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he established no standards of praise and blame, and the scholars mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 改右司郎中、集賢殿學士，卒。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Right Office and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the right office and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then died.

sentences.zh: 子登、冕。

translations.literal: Sons: Deng and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Deng and Mian.

sentences.zh: 芳子 登登，字成伯。

translations.literal: Liu Fang's son Deng—Deng, courtesy name Chengbo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang's son Deng, courtesy name Chengbo.

sentences.zh: 淹貫群書，年六十餘，始仕宦。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in many books, he did not begin official service until he was over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Thoroughly versed in many books, he did not begin official service until he was over sixty.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為大理少卿，與許孟容等刊正敕格。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he served as Vice Director of the Court of Justice and, with Xu Mengrong and others, revised and corrected the edict statutes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he served as vice director of the court of justice and, with Xu Mengrong and others, revised and corrected the edict statutes.

sentences.zh: 以病改右散騎常侍，致仕。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was changed to Right Regular Mounted Attendant and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was transferred to right regular mounted attendant and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十餘，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at over ninety; posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over ninety and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 登子 璟子璟，字德輝。

translations.literal: Deng's son Jing—Jing, courtesy name Dehui.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's son Jing, courtesy name Dehui.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，第進士、宏詞，三遷監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli era he passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations and was promoted three times to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli era he passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations and was promoted three times to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時郊廟告祭，吏部以雜品攝上公。

translations.literal: At that time for suburban and temple announcement sacrifices the Board of Personnel deputized persons of miscellaneous rank as the chief noble.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, for suburban and temple announcement sacrifices, the board of personnel deputized persons of miscellaneous rank to stand in for the chief noble.

sentences.zh: 璟據開元、元和詔書，太尉以宰相攝事，司空、司徒以仆射、尚書、師、傅攝，餘司不及差限，請如舊制，從之。

translations.literal: Jing citing Kaiyuan and Yuanhe edicts—that the Grand Preceptor should be deputized by a chancellor, the Minister of Works and Minister of War by Vice Directors, Ministers, Teachers, and Mentors, with other offices not meeting that threshold—requested return to the old regulations, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cited Kaiyuan and Yuanhe edicts—that the grand preceptor should be deputized by a chancellor, the minister of works and minister of war by vice directors, ministers, teachers, and mentors, with other offices not meeting that threshold—and requested a return to the old regulations; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Outer Department Secretary of the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to outer department secretary of the board of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文宗開成初，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era under Emperor Wenzong he became Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era under Emperor Wenzong he became a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 初，芳永泰中按宗正諜，斷自武德，以昭穆系承撰《永泰新譜》二十篇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fang during the Yongtai era had, while investigating the imperial clan register, traced from the Wude era and compiled the New Yongtai Genealogy in twenty chapters on zhao-mu succession.
