translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yongtai era Fang had investigated the imperial clan register, traced descent from the Wude era, and compiled the New Yongtai Genealogy in twenty chapters on zhao-mu succession.

sentences.zh: 璟因召對，帝嘆《新譜》詳悉，詔璟攟摭永泰後事綴成之。

translations.literal: When Jing was summoned for audience the emperor praised the New Genealogy for its detail and ordered Jing to gather and extend events after the Yongtai era to finish it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was summoned for audience the emperor praised the New Genealogy for its detail and ordered him to gather and extend events after the Yongtai era to complete it.

sentences.zh: 復為十篇，戶部供筆劄稟料。

translations.literal: He again composed ten chapters; the Board of Revenue supplied pens, paper, and stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He composed ten more chapters; the board of revenue supplied pens, paper, and stipends.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafting attendant of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，轉禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong acceded he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne he was transferred to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 璟為人寬信，好接士，稱人之長，遊其門者它日皆顯於世。

translations.literal: Jing was broad-minded and trustworthy, fond of receiving scholars; he praised others' strengths, and those who passed through his gate later all gained prominence in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was broad-minded and trustworthy, fond of receiving scholars; he praised others' strengths, and those who passed through his gate later all rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，再主貢部，坐其子招賄，貶信州司馬，終郴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang he again headed the Examination Bureau; because his son solicited bribes he was demoted to Secretary of Xinzhou and died in office as Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huichang he again headed the examination bureau; because his son solicited bribes he was demoted to secretary of Xinzhou and died in office as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 芳子 冕冕，字敬叔。

translations.literal: Liu Fang's son Mian—Mian, courtesy name Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang's son Mian, courtesy name Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 博學富文辭，且世史官，父子並居集賢院。

translations.literal: Learned and richly gifted in literary composition, and moreover a hereditary historian—in father and son both served in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and richly gifted in literary composition, and moreover a hereditary historian—father and son both served in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷右補闕、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He successively served as Right Supplements Clerk and Historiography Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as right supplements clerk and historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 坐善劉晏，貶巴州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Because he befriended Liu Yan he was demoted to Revenue Registrar of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he befriended Liu Yan he was demoted to revenue registrar of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 還為太常博士。

translations.literal: He returned and became Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and became erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 昭德王皇后崩，冕與張薦議皇太子宜依晉魏卒哭除服，左補闕穆質請依禮期而除，冕議見用。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhao of Virtuous Merit died, Mian and Zhang Jian argued that the crown prince should follow the Jin and Wei practice of ending mourning and removing mourning garments; Left Supplements Clerk Mu Zhi requested following the ritual period before removal; Mian's argument was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zhao of Virtuous Merit died, Mian and Zhang Jian argued that the crown prince should follow the Jin and Wei practice of ending mourning and removing mourning garments; Left Supplements Clerk Mu Zhi requested observing the full ritual period before removal; Mian's argument was adopted.

sentences.zh: 德宗既親郊，重慎祠事，動稽典禮。

translations.literal: After Emperor Dezong had personally performed the suburban sacrifice he again treated sacrificial affairs with great caution, and every move was checked against canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Dezong had personally performed the suburban sacrifice he again treated sacrificial affairs with great caution, checking every move against canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 冕以吏部郎中攝太常博士，與薦及司封郎中徐岱、倉部郎中陸質修飭儀矩。

translations.literal: Mian, as Director of the Board of Personnel deputizing as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, joined Jian and Directors of the Office of Investiture Xu Dai and of Granaries Lu Zhi in arranging ritual norms.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, as director of the board of personnel deputizing as erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices, joined Jian and directors of the office of investiture Xu Dai and of granaries Lu Zhi in arranging ritual norms.

sentences.zh: 帝疑郊廟每升輒去劍履及象劍尺寸、祝語輕重，冕據禮以對，本末詳明，天子嘉異。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned why at each ascent for suburban and temple rites one removed sword and shoes, and about the size of the ivory sword and the weight of invocation words; Mian answered according to ritual with causes and effects fully explained—the Son of Heaven commended him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned why at each ascent for suburban and temple rites one removed sword and shoes, and about the size of the ivory sword and the weight of invocation words; Mian answered according to ritual with causes and effects fully explained, and the emperor commended him warmly.

sentences.zh: 久之，以論議勁切，執政不善，出為婺州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time, because his remonstrance was forceful and pointed and the administration did not favor him, he was sent out as Prefect of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, because his remonstrance was forceful and pointed and the administration did not favor him, he was sent out as prefect of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十三年，兼御史中丞、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he additionally served as Censor-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he additionally served as censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 自以久疏斥，又性躁狷，不能無恨，乃上表乞代，且推明朝覲之意，曰：「臣竊感《江漢》朝宗之誼，《鹿鳴》君臣之宴，頌聲之作，王道本始。

translations.literal: Feeling himself long cast aside and moreover of a hot-tempered and narrow disposition and unable to be free of resentment, he submitted a memorial requesting a replacement and also expressed the meaning of promoting court audience, saying, "Your subject is deeply moved by the meaning in 'The Jiang and Han' of tributaries flowing to the lord, and by the lord-and-minister feast in 'The Deer Call'—the composition of hymns of praise is where the way of kings takes its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling himself long cast aside, and moreover hot-tempered and narrow by nature and unable to be free of resentment, he submitted a memorial requesting a replacement and also expressed the meaning of promoting court audience, saying, "Your subject is deeply moved by the meaning in 'The Jiang and Han' of tributaries flowing to the lord, and by the lord-and-minister feast in 'The Deer Call'—the composition of hymns of praise is where the way of kings takes its beginning.

sentences.zh: 國家自兵興，不遑議禮，方牧未朝，宴樂久缺。

translations.literal: Since the rise of warfare the state has not had leisure to discuss ritual; regional governors have not attended court and feasts and music have long been lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Since warfare arose the state has not had leisure to discuss ritual; regional governors have not attended court, and feasts and music have long been lacking.

sentences.zh: 臣限一切之制，例無朝集，目不睹朝廷之禮，耳不聞宗廟之樂，足不踐軒墀之地，十有二年於茲矣。

translations.literal: Your subject is bound by the catch-all regulations with no precedent for court assembly; for twelve years now my eyes have not beheld court ritual, my ears have not heard ancestral temple music, and my feet have not trodden the palace hall—twelve years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is bound by catch-all regulations with no precedent for court assembly; for twelve years now my eyes have not beheld court ritual, my ears have not heard ancestral temple music, and my feet have not trodden the palace hall—twelve years to this day.

sentences.zh: 夫朝會，禮之本也。

translations.literal: Court assembly is the root of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Court assembly is the root of ritual.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之制，群後四朝，以明黜陟。

translations.literal: Under the institutions of Tang and Yu the regional lords attended court four times to make clear dismissals and promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the institutions of Tang and Yu the regional lords attended court four times to make clear dismissals and promotions.

sentences.zh: 商、周之盛，五歲一見，以考制度。

translations.literal: In the flourishing age of Shang and Zhou they attended once every five years to examine institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In the flourishing age of Shang and Zhou they attended once every five years to examine institutions.

sentences.zh: 漢法，三載上計，以會課最。

translations.literal: Under Han law, every three years they delivered annual reports to court to convene for evaluation of achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, every three years they delivered annual reports to court to convene for evaluation of achievements.

sentences.zh: 聖唐稽古，天下朝集，三考一見，皆以十月上計京師，十一月禮見，會尚書省應考績事，元日陳貢棐，集於考堂，唱其考第，進賢以興善，簡不肖以黜惡。

translations.literal: The sacred Tang followed antiquity: the realm assembled at court; after three evaluations came one audience—all in the tenth month they delivered annual reports to the capital, in the eleventh month they were received in ritual audience, convened with the Department of State Affairs for examination of merit records, on New Year's Day presented tribute fabric, assembled at the examination hall, proclaimed their evaluation ranks, advancing the worthy to encourage good and selecting out the unworthy to dismiss the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred Tang followed antiquity: the realm assembled at court, and after three evaluations came one audience. All in the tenth month delivered annual reports to the capital; in the eleventh month they were received in ritual audience and convened with the Department of State Affairs for merit examinations. On New Year's Day they presented tribute fabric, assembled at the examination hall, and proclaimed their evaluation ranks—advancing the worthy to encourage virtue and selecting out the unworthy to dismiss the wicked.

sentences.zh: 自安史亂常，始有專地；

translations.literal: Since the An-Luo rebellion disrupted order, there first arose territorial autonomy;
translations.idiomatic: Since the An-Luo rebellion disrupted order, territorial autonomy first arose;

sentences.zh: 四方多故，始有不朝；

translations.literal: with troubles everywhere, there first arose failure to attend court;
translations.idiomatic: with troubles everywhere, failure to attend court first arose;

sentences.zh: 戎臣恃險，或不悔過。

translations.literal: military ministers relying on strategic terrain sometimes did not repent their faults.
translations.idiomatic: and military ministers relying on strategic terrain sometimes did not repent their faults.

sentences.zh: 臣忝牧圉之寄，憤不朝之臣，思一入覲，率先天下，使君臣之義，親而不疏；

translations.literal: Your subject, entrusted with pasturing the realm, resents those ministers who do not attend court, and thinks once to enter audience—leading all under heaven, so that the bond between lord and minister remains intimate and never grows distant;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, entrusted with governing the realm, resents those ministers who do not attend court and wishes to enter audience once—leading all under heaven so that the bond between lord and minister remains intimate rather than distant;

sentences.zh: 朝覲之禮，廢而復舉。

translations.literal: the rite of court audience, abandoned, would be revived.
translations.idiomatic: the rite of court audience, once abandoned, would be revived.

sentences.zh: 誠恐負薪，溘先朝露，覲禮不展，臣之憂也。

translations.literal: I truly fear carrying firewood yet dying before the morning dew, unable to fulfill the audience rite—that is your subject's sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that like one carrying firewood I may die before the morning dew, unable to fulfill the audience rite—that is your subject's sorrow.

sentences.zh: 比聞諸將帥亡歿者眾，臣自憚何德以堪久長。

translations.literal: Lately I have heard that many generals and commanders have died; your subject himself fears what virtue could sustain him for long.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have heard that many generals and commanders have died; your subject himself wonders what virtue could sustain him for long.

sentences.zh: 鄉國，人情之不忘也；

translations.literal: The homeland—what human feeling cannot forget;
translations.idiomatic: The homeland—what human feeling cannot forget;

sentences.zh: 闕庭，臣子所戀也；

translations.literal: the imperial court—what subjects yearn for;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial court—what subjects yearn for;

sentences.zh: 朝覲，國家大禮也。

translations.literal: court audience—the great rite of the state.
translations.idiomatic: court audience—the great rite of the state.

sentences.zh: 三者，臣之大願。

translations.literal: These three are your subject's greatest wishes.
translations.idiomatic: These three are your subject's greatest wishes.

sentences.zh: 」表累上，其辭哀切，德宗許還。

translations.literal: " He submitted the memorial repeatedly; its language was mournful and urgent, and Emperor Dezong granted him leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted the memorial repeatedly; its language was mournful and urgent, and Emperor Dezong granted him leave to return.

sentences.zh: 會冕奏閩中本南朝畜牧地，可息羊馬，置牧區於東越，名萬安監，又置五區於泉州，悉索部內馬驢牛羊合萬餘遊畜之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Mian memorialized that Fujian had originally been pasture land of the Southern dynasties, where sheep and horses could be raised; he established a pasturage district in Dongyue called Wan'an Pasturage, and also set up five districts in Quanzhou, requiring all horses, donkeys, cattle, and sheep within his jurisdiction—more than ten thousand head in all—to graze there.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Mian memorialized that Fujian had originally been pasture land of the Southern dynasties where sheep and horses could be raised; he established a pasturage district in Dongyue called Wan'an Pasturage and also set up five districts in Quanzhou, requiring all horses, donkeys, cattle, and sheep within his jurisdiction—more than ten thousand head in all—to graze there.

sentences.zh: 不經時，死耗略盡，復調充之，民間怨苦。

translations.literal: Before long they died and were lost almost entirely; he requisitioned replacements, and the people groaned in bitterness.

sentences.zh: 沈既濟沈既濟，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Shen Jiji—Shen Jiji, a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiji was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 經學該明。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was thoroughly versed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎楊炎雅善之，既執政，薦既濟有良史才，召拜左拾遺、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Yan greatly favored him; once Yan took power he recommended that Jiji had talent as a fine historian, and he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder and Historiography Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Yan greatly favored him; once Yan took power he recommended that Jiji had talent as a fine historian, and Jiji was summoned and appointed left reminder and historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 初，吳兢撰國史，為《則天本紀》，次高宗下。

translations.literal: Earlier Wu Jing compiled the national history and wrote Basic Annals of Empress Zetian, placed below Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Jing compiled the national history and wrote Basic Annals of Empress Zetian, placed below Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 既濟奏議，以為：「則天皇后進以強有，退非德讓，史臣追書，當稱為太后，不宜曰上。

translations.literal: Jiji memorialized his opinion, saying, "Empress Zetian advanced through forced possession and did not yield through virtue on retirement; historians writing retrospectively should call her Empress Dowager and should not call her 'Sovereign.'

translations.literal: Although Emperor Zhongzong was demoted to live in a princely residence, he embodied the primal origin and succeeded to the dynasty—he was originally our lord; he should be called Emperor and should not be called Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Although Emperor Zhongzong was demoted to live in a princely residence, he embodied the primal origin and succeeded to the dynasty—he was originally our lord; he should be called Emperor and should not be called Prince of Luling.

translations.literal: Before the Jinglong era Ruizong's mandate was not yet complete; he provisionally faced the great throne without justification in propriety—he should be called Prince Regent and should not be called Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Jinglong era Ruizong's mandate was not yet complete; he provisionally faced the great throne without justification in propriety—he should be called Prince Regent and should not be called Emperor.

translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zetian changed the Zhou calendar and established seven temples—the mandate was transformed.

translations.literal: Now to place Zhou beside Tang and list her as imperial annals, examined against the Classic of Rites, is called muddling names.
translations.idiomatic: Now to place Zhou beside Tang and list her as imperial annals, examined against the Classic of Rites, is called muddling names.

sentences.zh: 中宗嗣位在太后前，而敘年制紀反居其下，方之躋僖公，是謂不智。

translations.literal: Zhongzong succeeded to the throne before the Empress Dowager, yet the chronology of annals places him beneath her; compared to elevating Duke Xi—this is called unintelligent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong succeeded to the throne before the Empress Dowager, yet the chronology of annals places him beneath her; compared to elevating Duke Xi—this is called unintelligent.

translations.literal: Formerly when Empress Gao of Han held the regency, only enfeoffing the Lü clan as kings violated Han's covenant; there was no shifting the cauldron or revolutionizing the mandate. At that time Emperor Hui had already died and his sons were not of Liu descent—not recording Empress Lü—then with whom should one write?

translations.literal: Moreover Zhongzong at the year's beginning took the throne and at the year's end regained the throne; although his honored title was seized midway, the mandate was not changed—this suffices to head the annals by year; what constraint requires listing two annals?

translations.idiomatic: When Duke Zhao of Lu went into exile, the Spring and Autumn annually recorded his whereabouts saying: 'The Duke is at Ganhou.

sentences.zh: 』君在，雖失位，不敢廢也。

translations.literal: Request to merge the Annals of the Heavenly Empress with the Annals of Emperor Zhongzong; each year at the head one must record where Emperor Xiaohui was to unify them, saying: 'The Emperor is at Fangling; the Empress Dowager conducts affairs and changed such-and-such institution.

sentences.zh: 』紀稱中宗而事述太后，名不失正，禮不違常矣。

translations.literal: ' The annals would name Zhongzong while narrating the Empress Dowager's affairs—names would not lose correctness and rites would not violate the norm.
translations.idiomatic: ' The annals would name Zhongzong while narrating the Empress Dowager's affairs—names would not lose correctness and rites would not violate the norm.

sentences.zh: 夫正名所以尊王室，書法所以觀後嗣。

translations.literal: Correct naming is how one honors the royal house; writing method is how one instructs later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Correct naming is how one honors the royal house; writing method is how one instructs later generations.

sentences.zh: 且太后遺制，自去帝號，及孝和上謚，開元冊命，而後之名不易。

translations.literal: Moreover the Empress Dowager's final testament herself removed the title of emperor; when Emperor Xiaohui received posthumous title and in the Kaiyuan era received enfeoffment edict, thereafter her name did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Empress Dowager's final testament herself removed the title of emperor; when Emperor Xiaohui received posthumous title and in the Kaiyuan era received enfeoffment edict, thereafter her name did not change.

sentences.zh: 今祔陵配廟，皆以後禮，而獨承統於帝，是有司不時正，失先旨。

translations.literal: Now at enshrinement in the mausoleum and joint sacrifice in the ancestral temple all follow empress rites, yet she alone carries the succession as emperor—this is that the officials did not timely correct it, failing the former intent.

translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong acceded he was keen on governance.

translations.literal: Jiji remonstrated, saying, "The trouble with governance today lies in excessive offices, not in too few personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Jiji remonstrated, saying, "The trouble with governance today lies in excessive offices, not in too few personnel;

sentences.zh: 患不問，不患無人。

translations.literal: the trouble lies in not being consulted, not in having no people.
translations.idiomatic: the trouble lies in not being consulted, not in having no people.

sentences.zh: 兩省官自常侍、諫議、補闕、拾遺四十員，日止兩人待對，缺員二十一員未補。

translations.literal: In the two departments there are forty positions for regular attendant, remonstrance official, supplements clerk, and reminder; daily only two persons await audience—twenty-one vacant positions unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: In the two departments there are forty positions for regular attendant, remonstrance official, supplements clerk, and reminder; daily only two persons await audience—twenty-one vacant positions unfilled.

translations.literal: If one says the incumbent officials are insufficient for discussion, then others should be selected.
translations.idiomatic: If one says the incumbent officials are insufficient for discussion, then others should be selected.

translations.literal: If one wishes to broaden intelligence and gather the stranded, first fill the vacancies—why set up offices outside the offices?
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to broaden intelligence and gather the stranded, first fill the vacancies—why set up offices outside the offices?

translations.literal: Lending money for interest is a temporary expedient of officials and is not a method of classic governance.
translations.idiomatic: Lending money for interest is a temporary expedient of officials and is not a method of classic governance.

sentences.zh: 今置員三十，大抵費月不減百萬，以息準本，須二千萬得息百萬，配戶二百，又當復除其家，且得入流，所損尤甚。

translations.literal: Now placing thirty officials will roughly cost no less than a million per month; using interest to match capital requires twenty million to obtain a million in interest—assign to two hundred households, and they must also be exempted from corvée; moreover they would enter the stream of office—the loss is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Now placing thirty officials will roughly cost no less than a million per month; using interest to match capital requires twenty million to obtain a million in interest—assign to two hundred households, and they must also be exempted from corvée; moreover they would enter the stream of office—the loss is especially severe.

translations.idiomatic: Now the Guanzhong region is severely afflicted; everywhere people say that interest on public funds destroys families and breaks fortunes; it accumulates in prefectures and counties and has not yet been reformed.

translations.literal: Your subject calculates that the greatest drains on the realm's revenues and taxes are only two things: military supplies and official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject calculates that the greatest drains on the realm's revenues and taxes are only two things: military supplies and official salaries.

translations.literal: All other expenses together do not amount to one in ten compared with those two.
translations.idiomatic: All other expenses together do not amount to one in ten compared with those two.

translations.literal: Therefore the common people are heavily burdened and the spinning wheel stands empty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the common people are heavily burdened and the spinning wheel stands empty.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

translations.idiomatic: On all four sides the strategic situation makes armies impossible to dispense with; expenditures, though vast, cannot be avoided.

translations.idiomatic: Yet to add idle officials and redundant eaters—what harm is this?

translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell from grace Jiji was implicated and demoted to revenue registrar of Chuzhou.

translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Veritable Records of Jianzhong; the age praised his ability.

translations.literal: Son: Chuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chuanshi.

translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiji's son Chuanshi, courtesy name Ziyan.

translations.idiomatic: At the time Supervising Censor Xu Mengrong and Vice Minister of Rites Quan Deyu delighted in drawing carriage wheels with scholars and were styled "Quan and Xu."

translations.idiomatic: He was careful with penal law; whenever he judged cases he summoned his staff to weigh them evenly, and only when severity and leniency fully accorded did he pronounce sentence.

sentences.zh: 嘗擇邸吏尹倫，遲魯不及事，官屬屢白易之，傳師曰：「始吾出長安，誡倫曰：『可闕事，不可多事。

translations.literal: He once selected clerk Yin Lun, who was slow and unskilled and could not keep up; his subordinates repeatedly urged replacing him; Chuanshi said, "When I first left Chang'an I warned Lun, saying, 'You may leave affairs undone; you must not create too many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He once selected clerk Yin Lun, who was slow and unskilled and could not keep up; his subordinates repeatedly urged replacing him; Chuanshi said, "When I first left Chang'an I warned Lun, saying, 'You may leave affairs undone; you must not create too many affairs.

sentences.zh: 』倫如是足矣。

translations.literal: ' Lun was sufficient as he was.
translations.idiomatic: ' Lun was sufficient as he was.

sentences.zh: 」故所蒞以廉靖聞。

translations.literal: Therefore everywhere he served he was known for integrity and calm.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore everywhere he served he was known for integrity and calm.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎，卒，年五十九，贈尚書。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Minister of Personnel, died at fifty-nine, posthumously enfeoffed as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as vice minister of personnel, died at fifty-nine, and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister.

sentences.zh: 傳師性夷粹無競，更二鎮十年，無書賄入權家。

translations.literal: Chuanshi's nature was mild, pure, and uncontentious; over two circuits for ten years no letters or bribes entered powerful households.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi's nature was mild, pure, and uncontentious; over two circuits for ten years no letters or bribes entered powerful households.

sentences.zh: 初拜官，宰相欲以姻私托幕府者，傳師固拒曰：「誠爾，願罷所授。

translations.literal: When first receiving appointment, a chief minister wished to entrust a personal connection to his staff; Chuanshi firmly refused, saying, "If so, I would rather decline what I was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When first receiving appointment, a chief minister wished to entrust a personal connection to his staff; Chuanshi firmly refused, saying, "If so, I would rather decline what I was granted.

sentences.zh: 」故其僚佐如李景讓、蕭寘、杜牧，極當時選云。

translations.literal: " Therefore his subordinates such as Li Jingrang, Xiao Zhi, and Du Mu were foremost selections of the age.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore his subordinates such as Li Jingrang, Xiao Zhi, and Du Mu were foremost selections of the age.

sentences.zh: 治家不威嚴，閨門自化。

translations.literal: In managing the household he was not stern; the inner quarters transformed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In managing the household he was not stern; the inner quarters transformed themselves.

sentences.zh: 兄弟子姓，屬無親疏，衣服飲食如一。

translations.literal: Brothers, sons, and surname—regardless of closeness or distance—shared the same clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers, sons, and kin—regardless of closeness or distance—shared the same clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 問餉姻家故人，帑無儲錢，鬻宅以葬。

translations.literal: When asked for gifts for in-laws and old friends there was no stored money in the treasury; they sold the house to pay for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: When asked for gifts for in-laws and old friends there was no stored money in the treasury; they sold the house to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 傳師子 詢子詢，字誠之，亦能文辭，會昌初第進士，補渭南尉。

translations.literal: Chuanshi's son Xun—Xun, courtesy name Chengzhi, also skilled in literary composition; in the early Huichang era he passed the jinshi, appointed Defender of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi's son Xun, courtesy name Chengzhi, was also skilled in literary composition; in the early Huichang era he passed the jinshi and was appointed defender of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人，出為浙東觀察使，除戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Attendant, sent out as Military Commissioner of Zhedong Circuit, made Vice Minister of Revenue and director of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to drafting attendant, sent out as military commissioner of Zhedong Circuit, and made vice minister of revenue and director of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸通四年，為昭義節度使，治尚簡易，人皆便安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiantong he became Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi Circuit; his governance favored simplicity and the people all found it convenient and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiantong he became military commissioner of Zhaoyi Circuit; his governance favored simplicity and the people all found it convenient and peaceful.

sentences.zh: 奴私侍兒，詢將戮之，奴懼，結牙將為亂，夜攻詢，滅其家。

translations.literal: A slave privately served a maid-servant; Xun was about to execute him; the slave in fear banded with military officers to rebel; at night they attacked Xun and wiped out his family.
translations.idiomatic: A slave had a private affair with a maid-servant; Xun was about to execute him; the slave, in fear, banded with military officers to rebel and at night attacked Xun, wiping out his entire family.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Minister of War and Left Regular Mounted Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of war and left regular mounted attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉潼代為節度，馳至，刳奴心，祭其靈坐。

translations.literal: Liu Tong replaced him as military commissioner; he galloped there, cut out the slave's heart, and sacrificed at Xun's spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tong replaced him as military commissioner; he galloped there, cut out the slave's heart, and sacrificed at Xun's spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：唐興，史官秉筆眾矣。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Commentator says: When Tang arose, historians wielded the brush in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Commentator says: When Tang arose, historians wielded the brush in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 然垂三百年，業巨事叢，簡策挐繁，其間巨盜再興，圖典焚逸，大中以後，史錄不存。

translations.literal: Yet spanning nearly three hundred years, the work was vast and affairs numerous, documents and records multiplied; in between great rebels rose twice, canonical works were burned and lost, and after the Dazhong era historical records did not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet spanning nearly three hundred years, the work was vast and affairs numerous, and documents and records multiplied; in between great rebels rose twice, canonical works were burned and lost, and after the Dazhong era historical records did not survive.

sentences.zh: 雖論著之人，隨世裒掇，而疏舛殘余，本末顛倒。

translations.literal: Even those who wrote could only gather what the age afforded, and what remained was disjointed and partial, with root and branch inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who wrote could only gather what the age afforded, and what remained was disjointed and partial, with root and branch inverted.

sentences.zh: 故聖主賢臣，叛人佞子，善惡汩汩，有所未盡，可為永愾者矣。

translations.literal: Therefore sage lords and worthy ministers, rebels and flatterers—the good and evil surged mixed together, with much left unrecorded—this can be a perpetual sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore sage lords and worthy ministers, rebels and flatterers—the good and evil surged mixed together, with much left unrecorded—this can be a perpetual sorrow.

sentences.zh: 又舊史之文，猥釀不綱，淺則入俚，簡則及漏。

translations.literal: Moreover the style of the old histories was coarse and unorganized; where shallow it fell into vulgarity, where terse it missed and leaked.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the style of the old histories was coarse and unorganized; where shallow it fell into vulgarity, where terse it missed and leaked.

sentences.zh: 寧當時儒者有所諱而不得騁耶？

translations.literal: Was it that Confucians of the time had taboos and could not give free rein?
translations.idiomatic: Was it that Confucians of the time had taboos and could not give free rein?

sentences.zh: 或因淺仍俗不足於文也？

translations.literal: Or because remaining shallow and following custom was insufficient for literary craft?
translations.idiomatic: Or because remaining shallow and following custom was insufficient for literary craft?

sentences.zh: 亦有待於後取當而行遠耶？

translations.literal: Or was it also waiting for later generations to take what was fitting and carry it far?
translations.idiomatic: Or was it also waiting for later generations to take what was fitting and carry it far?

sentences.zh: 何知幾以來，工訶古人而拙於用己歟！

translations.literal: Since Zhiji's time, skilled at criticizing ancients yet clumsy in applying it to oneself!
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhiji's time, skilled at criticizing ancients yet clumsy in applying it to oneself!

sentences.zh: 自韓愈為《順宗實錄》，議者閧然不息，卒竄定無完篇，乃知為史者亦難言之。

translations.literal: Since Han Yu wrote Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong, critics clamored without cease; in the end it was revised and fixed with no complete chapter remaining—thus one knows that being a historian is also hard to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Yu wrote the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong, critics clamored without cease; in the end it was revised and fixed with no complete chapter remaining—thus one knows that being a historian is also hard to speak of.

sentences.zh: 遊、夏不能措辭於《春秋》，果可信已！

translations.literal: Ziyou and Zixia could not find words for the Spring and Autumn—is this not truly credible!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyou and Zixia could not find words for the Spring and Autumn—is this not truly credible!
